items.statement: Consolidated order backlog as of April 1, 2025 stands at INR 1636 crores.
items.quote: Our current backlog on April 1st, 2025, stands at INR 1636 crores.

items.statement: India business backlog is INR 549 crores, up 20% year-on-year.
items.quote: Our India backlog stands at INR 549 crores, which is higher by 20% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: India business EBITDA margin target of 15%-16% for next financial year.
items.quote: India margins will continue in this range as well 15 %-16% should be achievable for next financial year.

items.statement: UK Leven facility closure on track for Q2 FY26; all closure costs already taken in FY25.
items.quote: Our UK facility in Leven is on track for closure in Q2 FY’26. As you will see, in this quarter all costs accounted for this closure have already bee n taken in this financial

items.statement: Hyderabad facility shut down; production moved to Gujarat; closure costs taken in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: We also shut down our Hyderabad facility this year, and the cost of this closure was taken in Q3 of this financial year as well. The production from this facility has now moved to our facility in Gujarat.

items.statement: Poland facility offers ~30% cost benefit vs Western Europe; will improve group margins.
items.quote: if you had to ask me, you would see at least a 30% cost benefit between Western Europe and Poland, and that's something that we could expect that between India, Poland and the ot her value sourcing sites that we have, we will find the right kind of situation to make sure that the customer gets the right product at the right price point and we will improve our margin because of this low cost struct

items.statement: India demand improving: client plant utilization up from 45-60% to ~80%; pharma strong, agrochemicals expected to recover mid-year.
items.quote: In India, the conversations that we are having with our clients and these are owners, CEOs they are positive, like I mentioned all of them have said a similar statement that volumes have come back, their plants, which are running now at 45 %, 60% are now running closer to 80% so firstly, that's a positive sign.

items.statement: International demand uncertain due to tariffs; some projects delayed but pipeline robust; April order intake strong.
items.quote: In terms of global, chemical and pharma still continues to be below expectations. The uncertainty surrounding the tariff situation is obviously holding investment. However, some of these investments are being kind of discussed now. Some of these which have been pushed out are now kind of moving towards closure.

items.statement: Diversification into heavy engineering, mixing, systems, and new segments (food & beverage, mining, defense) to offset glass-lined cyclicality.
items.quote: The focus should really be on the othe r verticals, especially the non -glass lined verticals, the heavy engineering verticals and the systems verticals, where growth is really unlimited, because those market sizes, those addressable markets, are much, much bigger than what glass lined is

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty impacting international investment decisions; US tariffs may create opportunities via local manufacturing footprint.
items.quote: However, the current situation with the US, the tariffs, also the uncertainty surrounding investment that may have some impact on our international business.

items.statement: Repaid INR 116 crores long-term debt; net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.5x from 0.8x; net debt/equity to 0.2x from 0.4x.
items.quote: We have repaid long-term debt of around INR 116 crores, resulting in an improved net debt to EBITDA matrix of 0.5 times versus 0.8 times in the last financial year.

items.statement: Free cash flow INR 318 crores in FY25 (80% EBITDA conversion), up from INR 221 crores (50% conversion) in FY24.
items.quote: This results in an 80% conversion of the reported EBITDA of INR 381 crores. This is again an improvement over previous years where the free cash flow to EBITDA ratio was around 50%.

items.statement: Poland JV revenue to triple in first year to ~USD 5M; target ~USD 10M in 2-3 years; internal cost improvement play.
items.quote: Poland is a small entity that was a couple of years of startup, where we had 51% share acquired. Just recently the current revenue will be got tripled within the very first year due to the orders we are giving in there. The growth plan is to complete further buildings and increase capacity, and in just a few years it will double again and come close to the USD 10Mn within two to three years easy.

items.statement: India transformation program costs (INR 15 crores) and Hyderabad closure (INR 5 crores) fully expensed in FY25; no carry-forward.
items.quote: So the total number for the year is around INR 15 crores, that's the full amount that was paid to the advisors who are running th is transformation program. And on top of that, the INR 5 crores we spent on closure of Hyderabad that has all been taken in this financial year INR 20 crores in total, none of those costs will carry forward into the next financial year

items.statement: Expect better financial performance in FY26 vs FY25; India starting with 20% higher backlog and strong April order intake; international April also strong.
items.quote: We also believe that some of the agrochemical players will start investing in maybe August-September, time frame as well. So, all in all, we have a positive view on India starting this year already with a smart, a much bigger backlog than previous year, plus the first month especially April has been very strong in terms of order intake as well. So, we are in a strong position in India for the fina

items.statement: FGD (Flue Gas Desulfurization) new project conversations may slow due to regulation deadline push; existing projects continue.
items.quote: I do expect new conversations may get pushed out as customers potentially delay the capex that would go into these Flue Gas Desulfurization units, because regulation pushed out.

items.statement: Specialty film sales grew close to 10% in FY25 and expected to continue similar trend in FY26
items.quote: The company's specialty sales has increased by close to 10% in FY'25 and we expect similar trend to continue in FY'26 which will strengthen the business model.

items.statement: Sunshield and PPF combined revenue expected Rs.25 crore in FY26 and exceed Rs.50 crore in FY27
items.quote: So what Pankaj said is, sun control film and PPF taken together close to, we are looking at close to Rs.25 crore in FY'26.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue expected Rs.3500-4000 crore in FY26 with 10-15% jump thereafter
items.quote: This year, we are expecting anywhere between Rs.3500 to Rs.4000 crore sales, and a year thereafter, and the 10% to 15% jump.

items.statement: Full asset utilization of film business expected within FY27
items.quote: FY'27 the film assets will be fully utilized. And they will be greatly utilized within FY'27.

items.statement: Invested Rs.1180 crore in last three years across BOPP, CPP, polyester, metallizer, coating, Sunshield, PPF and rigid packaging lines
items.quote: The company has already invested close to Rs.1180 crore in last three years as capex in multiple growth projects including BOPP line, CPP line, polyester line, metallizer's and coating line, Sunshield and Paint protection film and rigid packaging.

items.statement: Additional Rs.200+ crore capex planned in FY26 for specialty capacity additions via internal accruals
items.quote: So there is additional around Rs.200 plus crore capex this year which will be largely done through internal accrual.

items.statement: BOPP film margin at Rs.21/kg in Q4 FY25, flat sequentially but up from Rs.14/kg YoY
items.quote: The BOPP film margin has been running at Rs.21 per kg in March ‘25 quarter, as against Rs.21 per kg in December ‘24 Cosmo First Limited May 21st ,2025 quarter and Rs.14 per kg in March ‘24 quarter, hence broadly at par with the previous quarter, but better on a Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: Specialty film margins largely protected; semi-specialty moves with commodity but lower delta
items.quote: Well frankly, in our past experience the Specialty Film margins broadly remain the same, except there may be some minor changes due to change in the mix. Semi specialty runs with a additional delta over the commodity. But the relationship is not linear.

items.statement: New BOPP line at 90% utilization and Rs.15/kg margin yields ~Rs.7.5 crore monthly gross margin; fixed overhead Rs.8-9 crore annually
items.quote: So new BOPP line would minimum generate, close to 90% utilization it would be close to 5000 metric ton monthly sales, even if we take the very subdued kind of the margins Rs.15 or so, it should generate Rs.7.5 crore of the gross margin on a monthly basis and fixed overhead on this line we do not expect more than Rs.8, Rs.9 crore on annual basis.

items.statement: Domestic BOPP demand growing 10-12% YoY to absorb new capacity
items.quote: But then, since domestic demand is growing 10%, 12% year-on-year, that should bridge the gap.

items.statement: Specialty vs commodity split at 71:29 in FY25; specialty split roughly 50:50 semi-specialty:specialty
items.quote: It keeps changing from quarter-to-quarter, but broadly you can say 50:50.

items.statement: BOPET currently 60% commodity, 35-40% semi-specialty/specialty; target to increase specialty share
items.quote: Right now, we do a mix of semi specialty and commodity and in the times to come our focus is to move more and more specialty, close to 35%, 40% is somewhere between semi specialty, specialty products.

items.statement: Four to five new BOPP lines coming in India in FY26 may cause temporary commodity margin pressure
items.quote: BOPPs concern this year in India, there are four, five lines coming up. So there may be a temporary blip, but as I said earlier, that our focus is largely specialty sales and specialty our margins are quite stable.

items.statement: Target to scale shoe business to INR1,000 crores revenue within a short time, but not in FY26
items.quote: our target is to be able to scale this up to INR1,000 crores within a short time

items.statement: Expect nearly 1/3 of gross block (INR650-700 crores) invested in ice cream business by FY27
items.quote: by next financial year, which is FY '27, nearly 1/3 of our gross block, which is close to about INR650 crores, INR700 crores, would have been invested in the ice cream business

items.statement: Shared manufacturing EBITDA margin target of 9% considered fair if sports shoe business performs as expected
items.quote: your understanding is quite correct -- quite fair, Akhil, that we can generate a 9% EBITDA margin in this

items.statement: Dedicated manufacturing EBITDA is absolute guaranteed number unaffected by top-line changes; shared manufacturing EBITDA margin expected to improve
items.quote: In case of dedicated manufacturing, I would urge you to look at the EBITD A number in terms of an absolute number and not as a margin of sales. In case of shared manufacturing, yes, you would look at it as a percentage of sales, and we are hoping and confident that we will be able to improve EBITDA to sales in case of shared

items.statement: Consumer demand remains weak with no improvement in April-May; still not out of the woods except possibly for shoes
items.quote: unfortunately, no. In case of some of the seasonal products, obviously, it helps. But then again, there have been rains, which have come in at wrong times at some of the places. So overall, I would say that it's -- still we are not out of the woods

items.statement: Ice cream factories (Lucknow, Nashik, North India) have 100% guaranteed volume offtake agreements under anchor tenant hybrid model
items.quote: all the 3 ice cream factories, the one in Lucknow, the one in Nashik and the one coming up in North India have guaranteed volume offtake agreements

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty on China creates cautious optimism for footwear exports and China+1 sourcing but too early to quantify
items.quote: we are, again, cautiously optimistic that based on the tariffs, et cetera, we are seeing some amount of increased interest in sourcing from India for the entire China Plus One thing working out, both in case of Footwear, in case of Foot Care and also surprisingly in case of Personal Care and OTC Pharma. However, early days, don't know how the entire tariff situation will pan out

items.statement: Shoe business turned PBT positive in Q4 FY25 excluding INR5 crore ESOP expense; full-year FY25 shoe loss INR11 crores including ESOP and integration costs
items.quote: we've lost about INR11-odd crores in total, right? And we said that, that INR11 crores includes the ESOP expenses

items.statement: Preferential allotment of up to INR5 crores in Kabadiwala for strategic EPR compliance advantage
items.quote: the proposal right now, Faisal, is to invest up to INR5 crores in Kabadiwala, which gives us a substantial minority stake

items.statement: Goal to double gross block to INR1,800 crores by end of FY26 from INR1,412 crores in FY25
items.quote: We continue to work towards our goal of doubling our gross block to INR1,800 crores by the end of this financial year

items.statement: South India footwear facilities targeting 30% of North production volumes by end of Q1 or Q2 FY26
items.quote: South facilities by the end of this quarter or latest by the next quarter will account for nearly 30% of the production, which is happening in the North

items.statement: Preferential share allotment completed in footwear subsidiary giving employees tangible stake; ESOP scheme rolled out at HFL for retention and leadership pipeline
items.quote: we completed a preferential share allotment in our footwear subsidiary, giving them a tangible stake in our collective future. Second, we rolled out an ESOP scheme at HFL aimed at rewarding high performers, enhancing retention and attracting the nex t generation of

items.statement: Management guides for 50% consolidated revenue growth in FY26 on a base of ₹425 crores, targeting ₹675-700 crores top line, with 20-22% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: We strongly believe we will deliver a 50% CAGR growth this year on the basis of this consolidated opening order. And then the year after, we are looking at a 25% to 30% growth because again you'll have the Monga Strayfield acquisition full impact coming into this year.

items.statement: Management expects 25-30% consolidated revenue growth in FY27, driven by full-year impact of Monga Strayfield and conversion of inquiry pipeline.
items.quote: And then the year after, we are looking at a 25% to 30% growth because again you'll have the Monga Strayfield acquisition full impact coming into this year.

items.statement: Consolidated order backlog stands at ₹483 crores as of March 31, 2025, with ₹160 crores in export orders.
items.quote: As a group, we have closed the year with an order backlog of ₹483 crores.

items.statement: Management expects ₹600-700 crores of order intake in FY26 based on 20-25% conversion of ₹3,000+ crore inquiry pipeline.
items.quote: On the order inflow front, as I said, we would have a conversion of around 20% to 25%. So if we're having a ₹3,000 crores pipeline, so you can expect ₹600 crores to ₹700 crores of order intake.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 20-22% for FY26, with Kilburn standalone higher, Monga Strayfield at 24-25%, and M.E. Energy at 15-17%.
items.quote: When we are guiding for between 20% to 22%, that is the range we are guiding at a consolidated level.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 is approximately ₹25 crores, but remains fluid and will be finalized in the next quarter.
items.quote: So as of now, I can tell you that we are targeting somewhere around ₹25 crores, but that is very fluid as of now. We haven't taken a call. Probably we'll need one more quarter to decide that.

items.statement: Inquiry pipeline has grown 50% to ₹3,000+ crores at consolidated level, with larger ticket sizes and new sectors like nuclear, cement, and pharma contributing.
items.quote: For the current financial year, we have an excellent inquiry pipeline of ₹3,000-plus crores at a consolidated level, and we hope to have a conversion rate of 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Nuclear orders now comprise 45-50% of Q4 order inflow; cement, petrochemicals, fertilizers, carbon black, and soda ash are key sectors for Kilburn; Monga Strayfield expanding in food and non-textile; M.E. Energy targeting cement and petroch
items.quote: We have inquiries from the nuclear. We have inquiries from the fertiliser. We're expecting some inquiries from petrochemicals, carbon black; soda ash, maybe, maybe not.

items.statement: Granules India order (~₹70 crores) is on hold pending pilot completion in 3-4 months; revenue spillover of ₹50-60 crores from Q4 to Q1/Q2 FY26 due to two incomplete projects.
items.quote: There's still one order which is on hold, where we had a large order from Granules which had come. We are still working with them on their pilot part of the order, which hopefully in the next three, four months should get completed.

items.statement: ₹200 crores to be raised via warrant conversion by June 2026; proceeds allocated to capex, term loan repayment, subsidiary investment, working capital, and general corporate purposes over 18 months.
items.quote: We have already taken our shareholder approval where the utilisation was mentioned. Part of it will go towards CapEx, part will be going towards repayment of our term loan. Part of that will be towards investment into our subsidiaries.

items.statement: Monga Strayfield expected to contribute ₹90-110 crores revenue in FY26; Ambernath factory fully operational, adding ₹100 crores revenue capacity; M.E. Energy Phase 2 expansion expected by mid-H2 FY26.
items.quote: Well, I would say that anything between ₹90 crores to ₹110 crores is what we are looking at, yeah. But as we go forward, we'll be more clear about the numbers.

items.statement: Export revenue target of 20-30% of total revenue in next 2-3 years, driven by all three entities (Kilburn, M.E. Energy, Monga Strayfield).
items.quote: We believe we should be aiming to do at least 20% to 30% of our revenue from the export space, which should be the target in the next two to three years.

items.statement: Management open to technology tie-ups in drying and heating solutions with companies in US, Europe, Japan; not dependent on acquisitions for growth but will evaluate value-accretive opportunities.
items.quote: We are in discussion for technology tie-ups, and we are in advanced stage for that. So every strategy for growth does not have to be inorganic. There are technology tie-ups which we are looking at with companies in the U.S., in Europe and in Japan.

items.statement: NSE listing approved by Board; timeline depends on NSE process, no specific date given.
items.quote: The Board has approved it that we are going to apply for the listing, then it is up to NSE to see what is the process and the time line, but we can't give a particular date.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations negative due to project execution timing, debtor buildup (₹30-40 crores billed in March), and ICDs to subsidiaries; management expects adequate capitalization and free cash flow generation going forward.
items.quote: In the last month itself of March, we have dispatched around ₹30 crores to ₹40 crores of billing has been done. So that has led to increase in our debtors also.

items.statement: Expects 10-15% revenue growth from all products, mix of volume and prices.
items.quote: We are expecting 10% to 15% growth in revenue from all the products. So, it is a mix of both volume and prices.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin more than 15% in the current year.
items.quote: In the last quarter i.e., in the fourth quarter of '25, we have EBITDA margin of approximately 13%. So, we are expecting more than 15% in the current year.

items.statement: Plans capex of INR150-200 crores for growth, infra, and automation.
items.quote: So, we are doing capex for INR150 crores to INR200 crores from the last 2, 3 years. So we have planned the same INR150 crores to INR200 crores in the current year.

items.statement: Aims to achieve more than 6% EBITDA margin from chemicals in current year.
items.quote: In the fourth quarter of '25, we have achieved 6% EBITDA margin from chemicals as compared to '24, 3%. So we are going forward to 10%. So hopefully in the current year, we will achieve more than 6%.

items.statement: Peak revenue from existing capacity is INR2,700-2,800 crores at current prices.
items.quote: So, considering the current price, the peak revenue from the existing capacity is something around INR2,700 crores to INR2,800 crores.

items.statement: Aims to scale export revenue to 40-45% over next 2 years.
items.quote: And we hope that in the year or maybe by the next 2 years, we will be able to achieve the export realization or export sale of around 40% to 45%.

items.statement: Chemical export revenue share increased to 18% in FY25 from 10-12% earlier.
items.quote: Earlier we were exporting around 10% to 12% of chemical revenue to the export market. After getting the recertification last year, the export revenue share of chemical business has been increased to around 18% during FY '25.

items.statement: Non-Ibu portfolio contributes about 34% to API revenues, up from 18% five years ago.
items.quote: This is a major step in strengthening our non-Ibu portfolio, which now contributes about 34% to the API revenues, up from 18% just 5 years ago.

items.statement: Paracetamol capacity enhanced to 10,800 MTPA with INR155 crore investment.
items.quote: This INR155 crore investment funded entirely through internal accruals has enhanced our IOL Chemicals and Paracetamol capacity to 10,800

items.statement: Expanded Clopidogrel capacity by 33%.
items.quote: We also expanded Clopidogrel capacity by 33% reflecting our belief in the long-term growth potentials of cardiovascular APIs.

items.statement: Acquired 101 acres for greenfield expansion; approvals underway.
items.quote: To support future growth, we have acquired 101 acres of land along the Chandigarh-Bathinda Highway, laying the groundwork for greenfield expansion. Approvals for industrial, environmental and NHI clearances are underway and progressing into FY 2026.

items.statement: Expects good volumes for Levetiracetam in near future.
items.quote: I think Levetiracetam, yes, the quantity will increase because we have already done some capacity enhancements for Levetiracetam also and we are approaching new customers as well and we have filed U.S. DMF for this product also. So we are expecting good vo lumes in near

items.statement: Ethyl acetate prices have bottomed out; demand may improve in 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: So, we think that the prices are already bottom out for ethyl acetate and now the demand is having some traction increasing maybe 1 or 2 quarters. So the demand side we can say that it may have some improvement, but price is totally linked with the prices of our raw material.

items.statement: Expects improvement in Paracetamol demand and price appreciation.
items.quote: For acetic anhydride, the prices are stable and for Paracetamol we are expecting maybe keeping in the current geographical scenario, there may be some improvement in the demand also with some price appreciation also.

items.statement: No plans for DCDA manufacturing due to input material demand-supply issues.
items.quote: I think as of now there is no plans to go for DCDA manufacturing because the basic input material is having some problem with demand supply, like this is basically Inaudible 48:52 product. So as of now, there is no plan to go for DCDA manufacturing.

items.statement: U.S. FDA inspection timing uncertain; company ready.
items.quote: I think U.S. FDA approval is clearly proceeded as per the regulatory or authority requirements, which means the company has nothing to do with the inspection. As and when they will plan for the inspection, they will come for the inspection.

items.statement: No capacity addition in FY26; capex will be maintenance and regulatory, not growth.
items.quote: So we don't foresee any capacity addition in the current financial year, which is FY '26. We would wait for the markets to kind of turn a bit and get our capacity utilization to about 80%, 85% before we get on to the next on capex cycle.

items.statement: FY26 capex for regulatory and maintenance is INR5-10 crores.
items.quote: So we are working it out, wouldn't be very large, INR5 crores, INR10 crores regulatory plus some repairs, maintenance kind of stuff.

items.statement: Expects H2 to be much better than H1.
items.quote: So we expect H2 to be much better than H1. That's one, if you ask me.

items.statement: Expects FY26 to be better.
items.quote: So we also expect FY '26 to be better. The Indian economy so far has been quite resilient to shocks from abroad.

items.statement: Premiumization will continue in FY26, improving ASPs.
items.quote: But I think even with extra trade discounting and all, we are confident that this premiumization would -- it is something which will continue for us in FY '26 as well. So that should do better for our ASPs.

items.statement: Retail demand has not yet shown dramatic recovery; H2 was slow.
items.quote: So not yet, Shubham. Nothing very dramatic. It's -- quarter 4 has been slow. Actually, the whole of H2 has been slow. So far, nothing dramatically different has emerged.

items.statement: Capacity overhang in Morbi expected to continue until markets improve.
items.quote: And however, there is more capacity, which is going to come online in Morbi in H1 in spite of the sluggishness in the market. So we expect this capacity overhang to continue till the markets turn for the better.

items.statement: Morbi producers attempted price increase of INR2 per square feet, but no effect yet.
items.quote: They have like kind of all the producers have taken or we are going to increase our price by INR2 per square feet, we swear by this, we swear by that, we do this, we do that. A lot of those videos have been circulated to the trade that our price is increasing, this-is-this, that-is-that.

items.statement: Exports uptick of 10-15% would boost domestic players.
items.quote: One is -- one piece of the puzzle is definitely exports. A small 10%, 15% uptick in exports will really give a fillip to domestic players like us.

items.statement: If exports rise 15-20%, domestic market will see traction.
items.quote: Now if exports go up by 15%, 20%, say from next month, you will certainly see a lot of traction in the domestic market itself because as soon as the capacity goes out, the pricing stabilizes, the dealers will stop postponing their purchases, builders will kind of stop negotiating forever and forever and start placing orders and all.

items.statement: Government vertical rebuilt; expects good results this year.
items.quote: The whole government vertical for us has been rebuilt from scratch. And we expect to see good results coming out of this year.

items.statement: Institutional sales are 20-25% of total.
items.quote: The way we track our projects, Moksh, we do roughly around 20%, 25% institutional one way or another way. This is a combination of small or medium or large projects, all of that put together, private plus government.

items.statement: Capacity utilization was 55-60% this year on expanded base.
items.quote: Now to answer your question, our capacity utilization last year was somewhere between 65%, 70%. This year is somewhere between 55%, 60%, yes, but on an expanded base.

items.statement: Own manufacturing capacity utilization about 55%.
items.quote: For our own manufacturing, I think it will be about 55%-odd, if I remember right.

items.statement: Market share is 5-6% of listed universe, 4-5% including top unlisted.
items.quote: So we would be about 5% to 6% of the listed company universe. If you were to add the top five or six unlisted players then the market comes to about INR15,000 odd crores and then you can get the numbers there. So it would be about 4% to 5% of that.

items.statement: US business expected to grow in single digits in FY26
items.quote: For FY26, we believe US will still grow in single digit.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to exceed or be around 26% in FY26
items.quote: So, F Y26, we believe , we will exceed 26 or around 26% comfortably in terms of EBITDA margins and that’s our current best estimate

items.statement: Overall revenue expected to grow double-digit in FY26 led by India and international markets
items.quote: So, for the overall business, we are looking at a double-digit growth in revenue led by strong growths in India and international markets, and also our new growth themes like biologics, vaccines, and all scaling up.

items.statement: India formulations business expected to continue outperforming IPM market in FY26
items.quote: We believe, in India, we will continue to outperform the IPM market for the year.

items.statement: Vaccines business expected to contribute meaningfully in FY26
items.quote: Yes, we will see some good contribution from vaccines for FY26.

items.statement: Emerging markets expected to continue strong double-digit CAGR and faster scale-up
items.quote: Emerging market has been consistently growing at a strong double-digit CAGR and also improving profitability. And that trend is also continuing and we are quite positive for a faster scale up.

items.statement: No major fall-off expected in US business in FY27 due to important launches
items.quote: No, I mean, see, we have important launches in FY27. So, assuming we are doing well with our approvals and regulatory front, we don't see any major fall-out.

items.statement: Base US business without exceptional products can sustain over $1 billion revenue
items.quote: So, I have always said that our base business, we believe without any of the one -offs, we can sustain easily over billion

items.statement: 14 to 15 important critical launches planned for FY27
items.quote: But, I said irrespective of that, we have a lot of important launches in FY27, almost 14 to 15 important, critical launches in FY27.

items.statement: Committed to making good amount of investment in US with foray into specialty
items.quote: But we have committed to making good amount of investment in the US with our foray into speciality and other areas.

items.statement: Digitalization and efficiency measures improved profitability by 50-70 bps, similar improvement expected going forward
items.quote: These measures have improved the profitability in the range of 50 to 70 basis points and we expect similar improvement going forward as well.

items.statement: R&D expenses on Saroglitazar to be at least 100 bps higher in FY26
items.quote: Plus R&D expenses upon Saroglitazar we would have at least 100 basis points higher than last year, at least.

items.statement: Wellness business took price increases and reduced costs in some products
items.quote: Wellness, we have been able to take some price increase also. We were able to reduce our cost also in some of the products.

items.statement: Strong base business growth in US with new contracts and requests for existing products
items.quote: We are seeing significant opportunities on our existing products in terms of new contracts and new requests.

items.statement: Expect 5-6% year-on-year LNG consumption growth and continued volume momentum
items.quote: So we expect our momentum to continue in that fashion.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR4,500-5,000 crores including INR2,500 crores for Dahej petrochemical project
items.quote: And we have scheduled capex program of around INR5,000 crores -- INR4,500 crores to INR5,000 crores in the current financial year, wherein the Dahej petrochemical -- for Dahej petrochemical project, we have targeted around INR2,500 crores of capex.

items.statement: Petrochemical project timeline end of Q4 FY28 for completion, production start Q1 FY29; feedstock is propane
items.quote: We'll be completing during the end of last quarter of 2027-'28, and we'll be ready with the production in the first quarter of -- last quarter of '27-'28.

items.statement: Qatar 7.5 MTPA SPA renewed for 20 years (2028-2048); downstream agreements with GAIL, IOCL, BPCL expected shortly
items.quote: On 6th of February 2024, we signed a contract with Qatar, wherein the 7.5 million ton has now been renewed for another 20 years from 2028 to 2048.

items.statement: Indian gas demand expected to grow 6-7% annually; space for all terminals
items.quote: Indian gas demand is expected to grow at 6% to 7% annually.

items.statement: PNGRB LNG terminal registration notification (May 8) reviewed; no major challenge foreseen on first reading

items.statement: Ind AS net impact FY25 INR13 crores positive; going forward positive barring forex loss

items.statement: Dahej expansion 17.5 to 22.5 MTPA expected ready for commissioning in 3-4 months
items.quote: we are expanding from 17.5 to 22.5 million tons and hopefully, within next 3- 4 months, we expect this to be ready for commissioning.

items.statement: Kochi-Bangalore pipeline expected completion by end of calendar year 2025

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR3 per share

items.statement: Expects Q-on-Q EBITDA growth to continue, with flow-through margins higher than revenue growth.
items.quote: We are not going to take a growth holiday. We've been growing every year. So if you see flow-through margins through EBITDA and PAT to be significantly higher than the revenue growth that we will achieve.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 to be much lower than INR245 crores.
items.quote: It will be much lower than the INR245 crores because we did a fair amount of spend debottlenecking the facilities for the next several years.

items.statement: Capex outlook for FY26 and FY27 to be similar or lower.
items.quote: The capex outlook, we expect to maintain similar or lower levels.

items.statement: R&D spend almost doubling, with $15 million of $20 million for Beyond $400 million strategy.
items.quote: So yes, it's -- we are almost doubling our R&D spend from where it was last year, and almost $15 million of the $20 million that we are spending will be for the Beyond $400 million play.

items.statement: Plans to file 3 to 4 products annually, mostly 505(b)(2)s.
items.quote: We expect to file about 3 to 4 products every year from -- starting from this year. And most of them are 505(b)(2)s.

items.statement: Expects 3 nasal sprays to be commercial in 12-18 months.
items.quote: All the 3 nasal sprays, we expect to be commercial between 12 and 18 months from now.

items.statement: Plans to reduce debt by INR300-500 crores annually, depending on R&D spend.
items.quote: And yes, maybe INR300 crores to INR500 crores is a range that we can look. Some years it will be INR300 crores, some years it will be INR500 crores. It depends upon the R&D spend that we are investing for the beyond $400mn strategy in the U.S.

items.statement: Will pass on tariffs to customers, no pricing pressure.
items.quote: We have no pricing pressure. We've been saying this for the last 3 years. We ha ve no pricing pressure because we exit if there is pricing pressure.

items.statement: Tariff ambiguity is a key risk, but U.S. growth trajectory unchanged.
items.quote: Risk compliance which for, so far, we've had stellar records for the last 20 years. I think we need to solve for the ambiguity of the tariffs. That would be kind of a tipping point. Not that it will impact us from our -- we are not changing our trajectory of the 400 million growth.

items.statement: U.S. business expected to grow, with $400 million objective intact.
items.quote: The U.S. business continues to be an important part of our overall growth strategy. Our $400 million objective has been up in our slides now for a good 3 years.

items.statement: Other regulated markets to improve, mirroring U.S. in 4-5 years.
items.quote: So, I think achieving consistency was a key theme that we have achieved. And I think going forward, although it's consistent 4 quarters, you'll notice there's a 13.5% growth.

items.statement: No one-offs in EBITDA; sustainable exit rate.
items.quote: You can, there are no one-offs.

items.statement: Average product launch revenue increased to $5 million from $3 million.
items.quote: Till about 3 years ago, our average revenue per molecule was about $3 million with 1 or 2 products exceeding $10 million. Today, our average product launch is $5 million, and we have several products which are more than $20 million.

items.statement: Net finance cost to be around INR160 crores next year.
items.quote: Yes. I mean our net finance cost for the year is INR195 crores, but we are exiting out at INR44 crores a quarter. And if you just extrapolate that, we will be within that range.

items.statement: Plans FY26 total capital expenditure of approximately Rs.1,300 crores, split into sustaining and growth capex.
items.quote: In FY26, we plan to incur a total capital expenditures of approximately Rs.1,300 crores comprising around Rs.500 crores in sustaining CAPEX and around Rs.800 crores in growth-oriented CAPEX.

items.statement: Guides annual EBITDA margin of 11% plus/minus 50 basis points.
items.quote: Despite lot of plants, which are coming in operational next year and also in the phase of initial growth, we continue to our guidance for an annual EBITDA margin of 11% plus/minus 50 basis points.

items.statement: Plans to spend around Rs.250 crores in FY26 on land bank in key automotive hubs.
items.quote: While we have built some strategic land bank in Kharkhoda and Khed, we are in process of continuation of building the same in other key automotive hubs such as Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar, Tamil Nadu and Gujarat for which we may spend around Rs.250 crores in FY26.

items.statement: Board approved Rs.423 crores investment in a dedicated facility for high voltage EV powertrain components.
items.quote: To support the growth of this venture, the Board had approved Rs.423 crores investment in a dedicated facility for high voltage EV powertrain components.

items.statement: Total estimated capital expenditure for relocation and expansion of lighting plants excluding land is Rs.233 crores.
items.quote: The total estimated capital expenditure for this relocation and expansion excluding land is Rs.233 crores.

items.statement: First phase of 60,000 wheels per month at Kharkhoda expected commissioned by Q2 FY26.
items.quote: Construction of our Greenfield facility is also progressing well at Kharkhoda , with the first phase of 60,000 wheels per month expected to be commissioned by Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Bawal two-wheeler alloy wheel facility targeted for commissioning in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: This facility is targeted for commissioning in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Phase-I of high voltage EV powertrain facility expected commissioned by Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Capital expenditure we face over next two to three years with phase-I is expected to be commissioned by Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Accounting policy change for casting tools will impact annual income statement by around Rs.40 crores.
items.quote: Estimated impact of the same is likely to be around Rs.40 crores on an annual basis, though a similar amount shall be reduced in depreciation over a couple of years.

items.statement: Expects at least 1.5x to 2x industry growth in coming year based on budgets.
items.quote: And with that, hopefully we should be able to deliver at least 1.5x to 2x growth in the coming year.

items.statement: Expects sensors and Westport businesses to grow at 1.5x to 2x of industry growth.
items.quote: So that business is definitely very promising and we do expect this business also to grow in terms of the outperformance, same 1.5x to 2x of the industry growth, we expect also this business to deliver.

items.statement: Remains optimistic on lighting business growth, expecting to grow more than 1.5x industry growth over three years.
items.quote: So we do remain highly optimistic in terms of like three years this business to continue to grow, more than 1.5 lakhs of the industry growth, which has been in line with our guidance as well.

items.statement: Sunroof annual peak revenue revised upwards to around Rs.230-240 crores.
items.quote: Based on the expected volumes indication, the revenues initially was estimated to be around Rs.160 crores, but that number has been revised upwards. So current visibility is that it will be roughly around Rs.230 crores or Rs.240 crores of annual peak revenue for sunroof.

items.statement: US tariff situation has no material impact as exports to US are less than 2% of total revenues.
items.quote: We would like to clarify that the ongoing US tariff situation has no material impact on our operations as exports to US constitute less than 2% of our total revenues.

items.statement: Approval of Rs.2,500 crores is enabling for both debt and equity, no clear visibility of long-term need.
items.quote: But going from starting, so the approval of Rs.2,500 crores is the enabling of approval, it is for both debt and equity, and as you would have seen, we have been taking the approval every year, even last year we had an approval of Rs.2,000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 volume guidance: 20 million tons grey, 22 million tons combined.
items.value: 20 million tons grey, 22 million tons combined
items.quote: So '26 volume guidance is close to about 20 million for the gray. And if you look at 22 million, it should be combined volume.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected Rs. 1,800-2,000 crores.
items.quote: CAPEX will be again in the range of Rs. 1,800 crores to Rs. 2,000 crores in this year.

items.statement: Premium cement share expected 15-17% in FY26.
items.quote: So for the quarter we have, I mean , achieved 15%, but we hope that we are working towards increase in premium, maybe another 2% increase overall, I mean, for the year the overall was about 14%. So we should do about anything between 15% to 17% in this year.

items.statement: Post-March cement price increase: 1% in North/Central, 5-7% in South.
items.quote: Post March if you see that North and Central there could be about 1% increase in the pricing, at least from the exit what we see. And in case of the South, yes, definitely about 5% to 7% increase is there in the pricing in the South region.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA per ton target above FY24 level of Rs. 1,087.
items.quote: But actually it will not be so as, I mean, yes on a year-on-year basis we will definitely be happy if we achieve a number which is at more than FY '24 the EBITDA per ton was Rs. 1,087, so we will be definitely happy if we are able to achieve more than FY '24 because FY '25 it was lower.

items.statement: Cost savings: exit Rs. 75/ton achieved; incremental Rs. 25/ton expected in FY26.
items.quote: And we feel that during this year also the exit, so we would get this Rs. 75 a ton benefit now going forward during the full year. The incremental benefit which this year we could get is maybe another Rs. 25, though the exit would be high.

items.statement: Green power share expected ~60% by FY26.
items.quote: So, green share. by FY '26 should be closer to 60, we are working out on various things. I think after Panna should be closer to 60.

items.statement: Paint business FY26 revenue target Rs. 400-450 crores.
items.quote: And again, we feel that in next fiscal again we should have a top line anything between minimum Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 450 crores.

items.statement: Paint EBITDA breakeven targeted by FY27.
items.quote: I think in FY '27 we should be able to achieve that , maybe it's one year extension because we bought the plant, so about FY '27 we should have a breakeven.

items.statement: UAE plant EBITDA expected Rs. 15-20 crores quarterly.
items.quote: Yes, yes, I said between Rs. 15 crores to Rs. 20 crores on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Incentives expected Rs. 75-80 crores per quarter in FY26.
items.quote: Actually incentive, we are booking on the accrual basis, so there's not much of a difference on the quarter-on-quarter basis, it is like normally in the range of Rs. 75 crores to Rs. 80 crores every quarter. And that is likely to continue in this year also.

items.statement: Asian Paints' white cement plant commissioning in Q2 may impact volumes.
items.quote: Asian Paints' plant is likely to commission sometime in Q2. And that will definitely have an impact on white cement consumption because they would also reduce the volume which they are taking from us going forward, because when their plant stabilizers, they will shift to their own production.

items.statement: Rural demand is good; demand driven by housing and infra.
items.quote: But in this month it is driven by housing and infra, it's a combination of all, we have not seen any. I cannot say that this particular sector is resulting in increase in demand, but rural demand is definitely good.

items.statement: Trade share focus; new markets like Bihar will be trade-only initially.

items.statement: Rail movement was 12% in the quarter.
items.quote: And our rail is 12% in this quarter, rail movement.

items.statement: Forecast U.K. revenue from India to grow minimum 3x within next 2 years
items.quote: We forecast that U.K. revenue from India will grow minimum 3x within the next 2 years.

items.quote: For FY '26 CAPEX plan, the Company plans to incur INR 250 crores for the year, out of which INR 130 crores for capacity expansion in Bangladesh and India: on Bangladesh of INR 110 crores and India INR 20 crores, respectively. items.quote: So that's why we have given a range of 10% to 12%. So just to mention that in the medium term, we are pretty confident of achieving this double-digit EBITDA margin.

items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA, excluding ESOP expenses, came in at INR 119 crores, up by 41.7% year-on-year, with margin at 9.7%. Excluding for losses in operation at new facilities, Guatemala, Bihar, adjusted EBITDA for Quarter 4 FY '25 stands at healthy double-digit 10.5%.

items.statement: India standalone Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin reached 10.2%
items.quote: Notably, India operation alone are now delivering a double-digit EBITDA margin of 10.2% in Quarter 4 FY '25.

items.statement: Tariff burden sharing negotiations with U.S. retailers ranged 1% to 4%, Pearl agreed up to 2.25% on 45-50% of revenue landing in U.S.
items.quote: But if specifically you are looking for what kind of discounts or burden share that these customers have been asking, that was varying from anywhere from 1% to 4%. For us, like wherever we have agreed to, it's not more than 2%, 2.25% is something that we have agreed to in some of the cases, not in all.

items.statement: Own designs contribute 40% to 50% of manufactured volume, design teams across manufacturing locations and key markets
items.quote: And we are proud that, okay, almost about 40% to 50% of what we finally manufacture comes from our own designs.

items.statement: India restricted Bangladesh garment imports via land route, but no impact on Pearl as no Bangladesh production enters India
items.quote: Now this particular ruling doesn't impact us because none of our production of Bangladesh was coming into India in any way. So we are not in any kind of impact or effect on this ruling for us.

items.quote: So this India revenue of INR 1,196 crores, and we already have built up a capacity to execute more than INR 1,600 crores, thus giving us the preparedness to accelerate the India business as the Free Trade Agreements of U.K. and potentially from European Union and U.S. are signed within this year.

items.statement: Guatemala productivity improved to 45-47%, targeting 70-75%, confident of cash breakeven within coming year

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target minimum 15% for FY26
items.quote: And the margin at the yearend will be in the range of 15% on EBITDA.

items.statement: Long-term growth target above 25% year-on-year
items.quote: definitely we will achieve more than 25% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: UAE entity revenue target Rs 235 crore for FY26
items.quote: So we will be, targeting Rs. 235 crores.

items.quote: So the debt equity what we have planned for funding this project is 50 -50, 50% equity, 50% is from the debt, which we had tied up with the bank and the one trench has been already disbursed.

items.statement: UAE facade manufacturing capacity 1 lakh sqm panel manufacturing
items.quote: So we had built a capacity of 1 lakh square meter of panel manufacturing, for unitized and semi-unitized.

items.quote: The toughening capacity is 15.6 lakhs sq.mtr. per annum. Two IG line having 6 lakhs square meter capacity, 1 laminated line with 1.35 lakhs sq mtr. capacity per annum.

items.statement: Order book sharing to start after Q1 FY26
items.quote: We will start sharing after Q1.

items.statement: UAE facade manufacturing operating margins expected 20%
items.quote: Operating margins will be in the range of 20%.

items.statement: Glass price reduction of 8% passed on to customers
items.quote: Somewhere 8% price reduction in the glass.

items.statement: Demand increasing due to strong real estate and infrastructure in GCC and India
items.quote: Demand is increasing because of the strong real estate and the infrastructure developments, both in GCC, UAE, or in India as well.

items.statement: IG glass sales increasing in India; laminated glass ramping in UAE; digital printed glass added via Glasstech
items.quote: We are increasing IG glass sale in India and the laminated glass also. And in UAE we are already using the product mix which is IG and laminate.

items.statement: Equity raise of around Rs 25 crore planned in 3-6 months for debt repayment and expansion
items.quote: The last what we were expecting to raise, around Rs. 25 crore from QIP.

items.statement: Plans to scale EWA partnerships from 60 to 250 during current financial year.
items.quote: We plan to scale this number of partnerships from 60 to 250 partnerships during the current financial year.

items.statement: Targets 250 corporates and Rs. 15 crores EWA disbursement by March 2026.
items.quote: See, we are targeting about 250 corporates. I think if we are able to achieve 250, we should have about Rs. 15 crores of disbursement by next year end, March 2026.

items.statement: Targets Rs. 15 crores EWA book and Rs. 110 plus crores business loan by March end.
items.quote: See, we are targeting Rs. 15 crores book by end of March for EWA and about Rs. 110 plus crores in business loan. That's the bare minimum.

items.statement: Aims to maintain ~100% quarter-on-quarter revenue growth from EWA program.
items.quote: So, on a quarter-to-quarter basis, our revenue from this program has increased by close to 100%. And we strive to maintain that percentage going forward.

items.statement: Sticks by previous profitability guidance and expects earnings growth as guided.
items.quote: But as far as the profitability whatever guidance we have given in the previous con call we stick by that. And I think hopefully we achieve what we are projecting in the last year.

items.statement: Raised Rs. 10.2 crores via preferential allotment of 7.6 lakh shares at Rs. 131 each.
items.quote: In the fourth quarter we raised Rs. 10.2 crores through preferential allotment. We issued 7.6 lakh equity shares at Rs. 131 each.

items.statement: Applied to State Bank to increase debt limits; plans to raise debt, not equity.
items.quote: No, no, no. We have already applied to the State Bank for increasing our limits.

items.statement: Bill discounting yields 17% plus 50% of processing fees.
items.quote: We get about 17% and 50% of the processing fees net. Let's say we lend to somebody at 18% or 19%, our share of the profit is 17% plus 50% of the processing fees.

items.statement: Business loans yield ~17% and EWA ~20% gross return.
items.quote: See, in business loans we are deploying almost 17% on average and EWA is about 20% what we are giving gross return on that.

items.quote: As on 31st March about Rs. 3 crores, we did Rs. 3 crores plus, now currently we are doing Rs. 3.4 crores.

items.quote: Of the total, so almost from Rs. 80 crores, Rs. 77 crores is business loan and about Rs. 3 crores is EWA as of now, this is on 31st March.

items.statement: Zero NPAs in FY25; focus on keeping delinquencies low.
items.quote: I am very happy to report in this financial year our NPAs are absolutely zero. In fact, we had very nominal NPAs in the last three years also, which was less than 0.5 in the last corresponding three years.

items.statement: Restricting exposure per corporate to manage risk.
items.quote: But we are restricting company wise elements. Even if certain let's say company is asking for Rs. 50 lakhs limit, we are just giving them Rs. 25 lakhs or Rs. 30 lakhs, we do not want to take too much exposure on a single corporate.

items.statement: Mobile app approved by Play Store, launching shortly.
items.quote: I am very happy to inform you that our mobile app has now been approved by the Play Store and we will be shortly launching it for the listing clients.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with Baya PTE for invoice discounting.
items.quote: We are also pleased to announce a strategic partnership with Baya PTE Limited Singapore for invoice discounting. This initiative will help us to support suppliers of large parties such as JSW Steel, Delhivery, PVR, Rickitt & Coleman, Haldiram among others.

items.statement: Net worth Rs. 75.10 crores; NSE listing possible after FY27 if maintained.
items.quote: One of the major reasons for coming out with the preferential allotment is the net worth should increase Rs. 75 crores, this year we have closed on Rs. 75.10 crores. So ‘26 and ‘27, if our net worth is more than Rs. 75 crores, we be eligible for listing on NSE.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 4.5% to 5.5% for the full year
items.quote: Yes., but the guidance is for the entire year. So we see cyclical changes, which happens during the winter. So that's the reason we are still maintaining the same guidance going forward.

items.statement: CNG volume growth guidance of 12% maintained for FY26
items.quote: I think we'll go by the same guidance for the growth, which I think we are maintaining a growth of 12%, and that growth will still continue in this financial year also.

items.statement: Spot LNG prices corrected from $13.5-14 to ~$12.7-13.2; propane landed price INR 43/scm vs PNG price INR 46.55/scm
items.quote: In the last quarter, the pricing was like close to $13.5 to $14, which has now come down by almost $0.80 or so in the last quarter.

items.statement: Morbi industrial volumes currently 2.6-2.7 mmscmd; expected to remain flat in Q1 FY26 with no major uptick
items.quote: So currently, we are doing 2.6, 2.7 in Morbi. Generally, we see I mean, spot prices have actually come down as compared to last year. But we also see propane prices coming down because crude has also come down. So I think volumes would be more or less same in the current quarter. We don't see any major uptick in Morbi volumes right now.

items.statement: CNG sales reached all-time high of 3.56 mmscmd in Q4 FY25; CNG vehicles grew 18% to 15.4 lakh

items.statement: APM allocation reduced to ~2 mmscmd currently from 2.3 mmscmd in Q4; NWG stable at 0.5-0.6 mmscmd

items.quote: And as we speak, the matter has been finally heard in Delhi High Court, and they have reserved the matter for orders. So matter will be finally decided by the Delhi High Court sooner.

items.quote: I'm happy to announce that Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR5.82 per share, that is to 291 percentage of the face value for a total amount of dividend outflow of INR400.64 crores.

items.statement: Business development policy approved for organic and inorganic growth including market expansion, partnerships, and sustainable energy solutions

items.statement: Plan to add ~70 CNG stations under FDODO scheme in FY26; 60 under construction/permissioning, 10 more to sign

items.quote: Birla Pivot has crossed annual run rate (ARR) of ₹5,000 crores based on exit quarter 4 FY '25 in less than 2 years of inception and achieved a 3.3x revenue growth over FY '24.

items.statement: Cellulosic fibre profitability lower by 12% YoY due to higher key raw material prices partially absorbed

items.statement: Birla Opus pricing at par with market leader in economy segment; competitors have tried price drops but factored into plan
items.quote: In terms of other aspects, yes, we have seen that maybe in the economy segment, some of the competitors have tried to drop some prices, etc, but those are all factored in the plan.

items.statement: Paint market excluding Birla Opus was negative in FY25; FY26 could remain low single-digit growth
items.quote: if you exclude Birla Opus, then the market has actually been negative. So, the market has actually been negative. And while it will be difficult to predict how FY '26 would go, but it could be that FY '26 remains a low single-digit growth here.

items.statement: Birla Opus luxury and premium products contributing more than 65% of revenue across all categories
items.quote: Our luxury and premium products are now contributing more than 65% to the company's revenue, a testimony to Birla Opus quality of products.

items.statement: Board approved final dividend of ₹10 per share, marking 62nd consecutive year of uninterrupted dividend payments

items.statement: Birla Opus reached high single-digit revenue market share in first 6 months of pan-India operations; combined with Birla White Putty crosses 10%

items.statement: Birla Pivot targets ₹8,500 crores annual run rate ($1 billion) for EBITDA breakeven; expects to reach faster at current growth rate

items.statement: Birla Opus targets ₹10,000 crores revenue in 3 years of full-scale operations for EBITDA breakeven; may breakeven earlier at ₹9,000-9,500 crores
items.quote: we said our ambition is to be ₹10,000 crores full scale 3-year operation and be EBITDA breakeven. Now whether I breakeven at ₹10,000 crores or whether I can be breakeven at ₹9,000 or ₹9,500 crores or somewhere in the journey in that ballpark range, we will manage it as we move ahead.

items.statement: Group EBITDA margin 17.4% for FY25, Q4 FY25 at 21.4%

items.statement: Carbogen CRAMS EBITDA margin 19.7% for FY25 vs 17.7% in FY24
items.quote: And for the full year, the margin stood at about 19.7% as compared to 17.7% in Financial Year '24.

items.statement: India CRAMS full year EBITDA margin 13% in FY25 vs near 0% in FY24
items.quote: And for the full year, this translated into a 13% EBITDA margin, which was almost 0% in FY '24.

items.statement: Negotiated significantly lower wool grease prices for Dutch subsidiary
items.quote: With the cost base, we looked into the cost base specifically into wool grease price, which is the most important starting raw material we work with, and there, we succeeded in negotiating new results in a lower price, much lower price

items.statement: Strong interest in CRAMS development pipeline, especially outside US and in ADCs

items.statement: Dutch business revenue mix shifted to 60% cholesterol, 40% vitamin D analogues in FY25

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 25% year-on-year for FY26, with EBITDA margin guidance of 17-17.5% for full year
items.quote: The guidance remains at 25%, all right. Now whether you take it as including other income or you take it excluding other income, so the guidance is 25%.

items.statement: Full year EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 17-17.5% on consolidated basis
items.quote: We have always maintained a guidance of close to 17% to 17.5% for the full year basis. We continue to do better.

items.statement: Order book at INR 10,545 crores as of March 31, 2025, with 68% public and 32% private sector
items.quote: Order book on stand-alone basis stood at INR10,545 crores as on 31st March 2025, with public sector accounting for 68%, while private sector accounting for 32% of the total order book.

items.statement: Order inflow of INR 2,823 crores in FY25, targeting INR 3,500 crores committed order intake for FY26
items.quote: Answering your question, the order intake, committed order intake for the current financial year will be INR3,500 crores.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 expected around INR 55-60 crores, similar to FY25's under INR 60 crores, plus temporary structures
items.quote: We had restricted our capex last year to under INR60 crores, I believe. And we would like to see a similar number in the current financial year, could be higher by about INR15 crores, INR20 crores.

items.statement: New accounting policy: no profit recognition until 10% of contract executed, impacting Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin by ~2%
items.quote: Starting Q4 onwards, the company has made a policy of not recognizing profits on the projects until 10% of the contract is executed.

items.statement: Profit recognition to resume from Q2 FY26 for NBCC and Signature Global Phase 1, Q1 FY26 for Maldives, Q4 FY26 for Signature Global Phase 2
items.quote: In Maldives from the current quarter for NBCC from quarter 2 and onwards, and even for Signature Global, because there are two phases in Signature Global, for Phase 1, we should start recognizing profit from quarter 2 and Phase 2, we will start recognizing profit from quarter 4.

items.statement: Bidding activity seeing significant uptick from both private and public sectors, expecting order awards sooner
items.quote: The bidding activity has seen a significant uptick, which should translate in order awarding sooner.

items.statement: Labor shortage identified as industry-wide challenge, influencing project mix toward less labor-intensive industrial/commercial/healthcare projects
items.quote: Obviously, the challenge will come from workmen and lack of qualified workmen, trained workmen in the country, which is an industry issue, and we all are finding ways to resolve that.

items.statement: Targeting net debt reduction to INR 120-125 crores by end FY26 from INR 195 crores currently, with INR 150 crores unutilized BG limits and INR 260 crores additional limits expected
items.quote: So on a net basis, if your debt level is close to INR195 crores today, we ideally would like to see that at about INR120 crores to INR125 crores.

items.statement: Focus shifting to industrial, commercial, healthcare projects; limiting residential due to labor intensity; comfortable managing 35 projects with minimum INR 10 crores monthly revenue each
items.quote: We will be focusing on industrial projects as well, more of commercial, more of health care, limited residential because y ou know that residential projects are very labor intensive

items.statement: MHADA project: 16 rehab buildings ongoing, 6 more starting June, 2 buildings delivery by June 10, sale towers IOA expected in 15 days
items.quote: MHADA project work on now 16 buildings of rehab are going on. Another 6 buildings, the work will start from June end. So that will make it 22 buildings out of the total 33 buildings. The first set of 2 buildings are being delivered for inauguration by

items.statement: CIDCO project: INR 2,600 crores across 6 locations, INR 1,100 crores billed, INR 1,300-1,350 crores balance over 18 months, Location 7 expected by Q2 FY26
items.quote: Location number 1 to 6 is INR2,600 crores. We have billed about INR1,100 crores. Submitted bills are close to INR200 crores. Balance revenue to be booked over there is close to INR1,300 crores to INR1,350 crores to be recognized over the next 18 months' time.

items.statement: Signature Global INR 1,200 crores project: Phase 1 started, Phase 2 expected by end Q2 FY26, revenue ramp above INR 20-25 crores from Q3 FY26
items.quote: Phase 2, the client has given an indication that will be made available by end of quarter 2. So you will see a ramped up revenue of above INR20 crores to INR 25 crores from quarter 3 for this project.

items.statement: Bank guarantee commissions reduced after investment grade rating, full impact visible from Q2 FY26, finance costs expected stagnant or lower
items.quote: What is interesting is after having gone into the investment grade, all the banks have reduced the rate of interest. And the rate of interest is not very interesting. What is important is that they have reduced the commissions on the bank guarantee and the full impact will be visible from quarter 2 of the current financial year, hopefully.

items.statement: Expect return to normal growth patterns in Kerala over next few quarters
items.quote: Based on this momentum and leadership team firmly in place, we anticipate a return to normal growth patterns over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Expect mid-teens growth for Kerala cluster in FY26
items.quote: But going forward, we are looking at least a mid-teens growth.

items.statement: Plan to add 2,100+ beds in India expansion over next three years
items.quote: We are significantly strengthening our presence in South India through strategic capacity expansion of the 2,100 plus beds year mark for India expansion.

items.statement: Bengaluru expansion of 939 beds including 430 beds at new Sarjapur hospital
items.quote: In Bengaluru, Aster will add a total of 939 beds, including 350 beds at Aster CMI hospitals, another 159 beds at Aster Whitefield, and 430 beds at the newly announced fourth hospital on Sarjapur Road, with 300 beds expected by H2 of FY27 and the remaining 130 beds by F Y29.

items.statement: Kerala expansion of 818 beds via two greenfield projects
items.quote: In Kerala, we will add 818 beds over the next three years with two major greenfield projects, Aster Kasargod, a 264-bed hospital, and Aster Capital in Trivandrum, a 454-bed facility.

items.statement: Hyderabad 300-bed Women and Children Hospital planned
items.quote: and in Hyderabad, a 300-bed state of the art Women and Children Hospital are planned to be commissioned.

items.statement: Quality Care to add 1,200 new beds over next three years
items.quote: In terms of network expansion, we are on track to add 1,200 new beds over the next three years, a 25% increase in capacity.

items.statement: FY25 capex investment of INR 342 crores
items.quote: We have made a capital expenditure investment of INR 342 crores while maintaining our gross debt at lower levels than the last year at INR 642 crores.

items.statement: FY25 operating EBITDA margin expanded to 19.5% from 16.8%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA grew by 30% reaching INR 806 crores, with EBITDA margins expanding to 19.5% in FY25, up from 16.8% just a year ago.

items.statement: Mature hospitals EBITDA margin 24.3% with ROCE 34%
items.quote: Specifically, our mature hospitals, those that have been operational for more than six years, have expanded their EBITDA margin to 24.3% in FY25, up from 22.4% a year ago with the return of capital employed of 34%.

items.statement: Karnataka-Maharashtra cluster EBITDA margin 28.8% in FY25
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA margin expanded to 28.8% in FY25, up from 19.7% in the previous year.

items.statement: Kerala cluster EBITDA margin improved to 23.4% in FY25

items.statement: Andhra-Telangana cluster EBITDA margin strengthened to 12.7%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA rose sharply by 45%, moving from INR 41 crore in FY24 to INR 60 crores in FY25, with the margin strengthening from 10% to 12.7%.

items.statement: Ramadan caused 2.5-3% revenue hit in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, we believe that almost 2.5%-3% of the revenue hit has been caused because of the Ramadan impact.

items.statement: Merger with Quality Care expected to complete by Q4 FY26 pending NCLT and stock exchange approvals
items.quote: The transaction now awaits final regulatory clearances, including approvals from the stock exchanges and the NCLT, and it is expected to be complete by Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Target 23-24% EBITDA margin in next 3-4 years including QCIL synergies
items.quote: we are also aiming to reach 23-24% in next 3-4 years' timeline. So, we are very much committed in this regard.

items.statement: Expect high single digit volume growth of 7-8% going forward
items.quote: we are back to high single digit volume growth is something which we are make it

items.statement: Full year EBITDA margins of 19.3% are sustainable; hospital segment margin could be 100-200 bps higher than group 23-24% target
items.quote: what I can say is that going forward also on a full year basis, these numbers what we published is more of a sustainable.

items.statement: 2,100 beds in pipeline costing ~INR 1,900 crore; INR 350-400 crore already spent; balance INR 1,500 crore over next 3-4 years
items.quote: We have 2,100 beds in pipeline, which will cost me approximately INR 1,900 crores. Out of INR 1,900 crores, we already incurred INR 350 to 400 crores. So, balance INR 1,500 crores, which we need to spend over a period of next three to four years

items.statement: QCIL expansion capex to be funded ~70% by debt at entity level
items.quote: we're looking at raising some debt at the entity level. And my sense currently, I may not have the exact numbers, is about 70% of what we'll invest in the project, CapEx.

items.statement: Price increase of 3-3.5% on ARPOB across payor mix; insurance renewed every two years
items.quote: the price increase would be somewhere between 3 - 3.5%. That's a price increase. That's how I'm saying cumulative of the walk-in cash patients plus the TPAs.

items.statement: Greenfield hospitals break-even at ~30% occupancy; Bangalore third hospital broke even in 3 months due to brand recall
items.quote: it's usually 30% you should be able to break-even Nikhil. I'm talking about on a full capacity basis if it's operational on a 30% capacity, you should be able to break even.

items.quote: Maldives, we've seen major ramp up in the business in last year and we have also seen that they are not very good paymasters. We had to control the receivables and that's where you also see in the Q4 because we were able to reduce the Maldives, the business very consciously.

items.statement: Non-Aster lab business target 36-38% in FY26 from 28% in FY25; labs margin at 7-8% currently, targeting 20% at 40-50% non-Aster mix
items.quote: year a lot of consolidations happened in terms of the ramp up of the lot of FPECs which 24 Aster DM Healthcare Limited – Q4 and full year FY25 Earnings Conference Call we opened up. So we look at somewhere between 36 to 38% is the non- Aster business which we want to drive in the

items.statement: Hyderabad women and child hospital delayed to Q2 FY27 due to warm shell infrastructure work
items.quote: We'll be able to ensure that we could kick off the project and by 2027 we are very positive. At least the second quarter at least we should be able to kickstart the hospital.

items.statement: QCIL FY26 synergy target INR 50-60 crore; INR 20 crore run-rate achieved in Q4 from procurement and other initiatives
items.quote: INR 50 to 60 crores is the synergy number that we're looking at the QCIL level. And this is outside of synergies that will be driven post the merger.

items.statement: Pre-IndAS rental cost (fixed + variable) ~INR 124 crore or 2.5-3% of revenue for next 3-4 years; variable rent ~INR 8 crore/quarter
items.quote: both fixed and variable, you can model it out somewhere between 2.5% to 3% for the next three to four years.

items.statement: Solar plants of 30-32 MW in progress to kick in H2 FY26 for electricity cost savings
items.quote: We are already in the way to bring more than, I think, 30-32 megawatt plants, which is in the works today. So that is something which is going to kick in sometime in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Andhra cluster occupancy dip due to clinician attrition in Guntur and Ongole; being rectified with new hires
items.quote: We had two or three clinicians moving because of competition, and we are quickly filling up that, and it will happen. And we have already onboarded one or two clinicians and adding a few more and augment, and we are trying to ramp up the place as well.

items.statement: Manpower cost efficiency improved 70 bps in FY25; further 1-1.2% per occupied bed efficiency possible
items.quote: even in the current year, from the last year to current year, when we say manpower cost, I'm talking about including the junior doctors plus the employees and the outsource manpower. We already done a 70 bps efficiency reduction in the current year.

items.statement: Double-digit volume growth expected for FY26
items.quote: So I think this year, we should have double-digit volume growth, given that last year was a tough year.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance maintained at around 12%
items.quote: So over the long term, we would still maintain our guidance of around 12% EBITDA margin for the long term.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR220 crores including INR70 crores for Bihar completion, INR43 crores for Aquel, INR7-8 crores for Bhuj, and INR100 crores maintenance
items.quote: So around INR220 crores will be the capex planned for FY '26 and in this, only INR100 crores is related to ongoing maintenance of plants and INR120 crores is one-off, which will give us a good capacity expansion in both Bathware as well as pipes and fittings in East India.

items.statement: Begusarai Phase 1 commissioned with 24,000 MT capacity; full 60,000 MT within 6 months
items.quote: The balance capacity at Begusarai is expected to be commissioned with full capacity within the next 6 months.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 inventory loss of INR25 crores; full year INR85-90 crores
items.quote: So it is around INR25 crores for this quarter, the inventory loss.

items.statement: Bathware Q4 FY25 revenue INR10.5 crores, loss INR4.5 crores; full year revenue INR30 crores, loss INR17-18 crores
items.quote: And for -- if you talk about this quarter, the sale was around INR10.5 crores and loss for this quarter was in the range of INR4.5 crores.

items.statement: Industry volume flat in Q4 FY25, slight degrowth for full year; FY26 industry growth expected at 5-7% led by CPVC
items.quote: I think Q4 has been flattish for the industry. I think for full year, there has been a slight degrowth for the plastic piping industry.

items.statement: PVC prices bottomed out; recent INR1,500/MT increase by Reliance; expect stable range-bound prices around INR75-80/kg
items.quote: I think PVC will continue to be range bound, but you will see a recovery. So whatever PVC today is maybe around INR70 per kg, this could move to around INR75 to INR80 a kg.

items.statement: CPVC grew double-digit in Q4 and FY25; drove realization and margin improvement
items.quote: Yes, we have had a better sale of value-added products, CPVC specifically. So we have been growing in CPVC at a good pace relative to PVC, and that trend has continued in the March quarter.

items.statement: Channel inventory low at <2 weeks vs normal 3-4 weeks; no aggressive restocking expected
items.quote: Channel inventory as we speak is low for my channel partners because of the reluctance to stock material. So channel inventory is low.

items.statement: Raw material inventory to normalize to 30 days by end of Q1 or early Q2; finished goods inventory to stay at 30-40 days
items.quote: Raw material inventory will normalize by the end of this quarter or the beginning of Q2, and we will continue to then have a tight control on the raw material inventory.

items.statement: Bathware breakeven expected in 4-5 quarters (FY26)
items.quote: I think another 4 to 5 quarters.

items.statement: Ad spend maintained at ~2% of sales; INR53 crores in FY25, similar planned for FY26
items.quote: As we have always maintained, means around 2% is something what we are maintaining. And we'll keep on having the same number for the next year also.
