items.quote: Currently, I think we are not evaluating OPVC. We are focusing more on new products, which will be for the retail and the private B2B projects.

items.statement: Begusarai plant to contribute 20-25 KT in FY26; ideal utilization in 24-36 months
items.quote: So I think this year, we could see around 20 Kt to 25 Kt coming in from the Begusarai facility. And maybe from FY '27 onwards, we would see closer to ideal capacity utilization.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at double digits with exports growing 50%+ and domestic contributing the rest
items.quote: We will grow by double digits, sir. For this year, the higher growth will come from our export business.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin target to improve by at least 100 bps from FY25's 38.1% despite export mix dilution
items.quote: We wish to improve our gross margin at least by 1%. And we also want to improve our EBITDA margins at least by 1% in the current year.

items.statement: Annual capex limited to Rs 25 crore for manufacturing plus tooling; total outlay including retail deposits not exceeding Rs 40 crore
items.quote: I think going forward, apart from our retail store expansion and tooling, we don't see a plan of investing more than Rs. 25 crores annually.

items.statement: Strong export order book for ceramic-coated cookware, cast iron, and outdoor grills; IKEA supply to start end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: We have a robust demand, but because of this new coating system that we have implemented for the cookware, we are ramping up our capability to manufacture them.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin 38.1% (+120 bps YoY), EBITDA margin 10.4% (+170 bps); Q4 gross margin 38.6% (+150 bps), EBITDA margin 9.4% (+180 bps)
items.quote: Through disciplined execution and cost optimization, we achieved gross margins of 38.1% for the full year. Our EBITDA margin also saw a healthy improvement, expanding to 10.4% in FY'25 compared to 8.7% in the previous fiscal.

items.statement: Price increases implemented every quarter alongside efficiency gains; domestic products aggressively priced with room for further hikes
items.quote: We continue to improve on our margins. It's a function of both efficiency improvement and some price increase post that. And we continue to do this every quarter.

items.statement: Q4 demand soft across GT, institutional and microfinance channels; early rural recovery signs; urban consumption expected to follow
items.quote: The quarter was a subdued quarter. It was not as per our plan. There was softness in the demand.

items.statement: Export share to rise from 11% to 25% in 3 years; ceramic cookware, cast iron, outdoor grills, chimneys, OTGs and IKEA bakeware driving mix shift
items.quote: From the last year, we were at about 12% contribution to our overall revenue. In the next three years, we will be sure it will cross 25%.

items.statement: Tariffs on China seen as positive for India sourcing; all export pricing FOB so tariffs do not impact company
items.quote: The tariff is actually a positive for a country like India. There is a strategy by many of these retailers that they would want to look at an alternate or additional source other than China.

items.statement: Retail expansion to add 90-100 COFO/FOFO stores in FY26 (~25 per quarter); COCO capped at 171; new stores EBITDA-negative initially but accretive at maturity
items.quote: This year we hope to add another 90 stores to 100 stores. So every quarter we will endeavor to open around 25 stores.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity now supports Rs 2,500 cr revenue (95% in-house); cast iron foundry commissioned at 2.2M pcs scalable to 4.4M
items.quote: You are right. 2,500 crore of prod uction, production revenue. So we will continue to still have some revenue outside of the production

items.statement: Lease accounting added Rs 9.5 cr extra charge vs actual rent in FY25 (Rs 3.4 cr in Q4); difference reverses after year 5
items.quote: For the whole year, the approximate difference between the rental and the lease accounting is about 9.5 crores.

items.statement: Management expects to return to historical growth rates of 25% to 30% plus from FY26 onwards
items.quote: we should be coming back to our historical growth rates, which h ave been in the range of 25% to 30% plus. And I think we should be able to continue to see that kind of a growth from '26 onwards

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided at 26% to 28% for FY26, consistent with historical range
items.quote: we expect that the newer products should also give us a similar kind of a margin range, 26% to 28%, which historically we've been guiding.

items.statement: Completed nearly INR670 crores of planned capex with two facilities commercialized and one ready for commercialization next quarter
items.quote: As of March 31st, we have completed nearly INR670 c rores of the planned capex, two manufacturing facility already commercialized and 1 new manufacturing facility ready for commercialization in the upcoming quarter

items.statement: Agrochemical sector showing signs of revival with ramp-up of key AI molecule and recovery in existing molecule volumes
items.quote: The agrochemical sector, which faced demand challenges in the earlier part of the year, has started to show signs of revival. This is further strengthened by the ramp-up of a recently launched key molecule in the agrochemical segment, coupled with the recovery in volumes of existing molecules.

items.statement: Pharma expected at 20-25% of FY26 revenue, Performance Chemicals at 25%+, Personal Care at 8-10%, balance from Agro
items.quote: today, if you look at Pharma is around abou t 20% plus of our revenue. We expect that, that should be 20% to 25% of our revenue next year on an expanded base. In terms of performance chemicals, it is around about 15% plus in 2025. We should expect 25-plus percent of FY '26 revenue on an expanded revenue base

items.statement: Working capital intensity targeted to reduce to 200 days (+/-20) by FY27 with long-term debt practically zero after warrant conversion
items.quote: we would be looking at coming to around about 200-odd days, plus or minus 20 days of my working capital. That's what I have -- we as management have a target for us, one. Long-term debt will be practically zero because that should largely be done through -- with the warrants conversion by this year itself.

items.statement: Revenue decline in FY25 was volume-driven with minimal pricing impact; raw material costs stable at 30-40% of total costing
items.quote: largely this degrowth, if you see on an annual basis is largely on account of volume. Very, very limited will be really on the price impact.

items.statement: H1 FY26 expected at 40-45% of full year revenue, H2 at 55-60% due to product ramp-up and industry cyclicality
items.quote: I think H1, we should be looking at around about 40%, 45% of th e total year's revenue, which also is typically the kind of numbers that we have been his torically seeing because of cyclicity of the industry. And H2 will be around about 55% to 60

items.statement: INR185 crores of long-term debt to be repaid through warrant conversion proceeds in FY26
items.quote: The proceeds from warrant conversion expected in F Y '26 will be utilized to repay long-term debt. Approximately INR185 crores of long-term debt will be settled through this route, significantly aiding to deleverage the balance

items.statement: AI molecule in agrochemicals has 2,800 metric ton market size, triple-digit dollar per kg pricing, customer targeting 5-10% market share
items.quote: this AI is having a pricing of tri ple digit in dollar terms in kg. And also, this is a large molecule with a 2,800 metric ton of the total market size. Our customer is expecting around 5% to 10% of revenue -- sorry, market share of that

items.statement: Current gross block plus new plant can support INR3,000-3,500 crores revenue; battery chemical may need additional capex later
items.quote: current gross block, if I add the new plant as well, INR3,000 crores plus to INR3,500 crores plus kind of a revenue is expected -- can be expect ed from these products

items.statement: Incremental working capital for new contracts estimated at 150-180 days
items.quote: Yes. You can take it as 150 to 180 days.

items.statement: Committed to 15% revenue CAGR guidance
items.quote: And with that, we remain committed to our guidance of 15% CAGR.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance 55-57%, EBITDA ~30%, PAT ~15%
items.quote: broad guidance, as we have always given, gross margin in that range of 55% to 57%, EBITDA in that range of around 30% and PAT around 15% is what we would continue to endeavor to achieve.

items.statement: Warehouse investment of ~INR40 crore cash outflow expected in H1 FY26
items.quote: that cash outflow should happen in current year. Most probably, most of it will happen in the H1 of this current financial year.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 31%, in line with guidance
items.quote: Additionally, our EBITDA for the quarter came in at 31%, in line with our guidance.

items.statement: Gross margins running in high 50% range, above ~55% guidance
items.quote: Our gross margins remain healthy running in the high 50% range and above our guidance of approximately 55%.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment settling into steady state; 2 quarters of double-digit growth
items.quote: we're seeing the consumer sentiment settle into now a pattern that I would say is more reflective of a steady state of business as opposed to the lumpiness of the post-COVID highs and the post-COVID lows.

items.statement: No significant price hikes planned for FY26; input costs stable
items.quote: Not specifically, we are not seeing a significant increase in our input costs. So broadly, what we will see is the mix of some cost increase and predominantly mix change.

items.statement: Plan to open more Fila stores in H2 FY26; Foot Locker expansion slowed until BIS visibility improves
items.quote: we definitely intend to open more stores in H2 of this year, right, in fiscal H2 of this year. And that's definitely staying on track.

items.statement: BIS certification still a challenge for Foot Locker and Fila; not all production duplicated in India
items.quote: even as far as BIS goes, while we've been able to duplicate a lot of the production to India, it's not everything either. So that is still a challenge for our Foot Locker and our Fila business.

items.statement: Fila EBITDA loss reduced ~50% YoY from INR58 crore; further improvement expected
items.quote: last year, if you remember, overall loss that we had posted for Fila was around INR58 crores. This year, we have been able to reduce this amount significantly, somewhere closer about 50-odd percent.

items.statement: E-commerce grew 45% in Q4, 20% for FY25; contribution ~10.6%, may rise 1-2% in FY26
items.quote: it is 10.6%, maybe if you force me to put a number, maybe I'll say it will increase by 1% or 2% in the coming year or so.

items.statement: Balance sheet solid with INR775 crore treasury; annual cash accrual sufficient for store expansion
items.quote: If you see our balance sheet, we have a treasury of around INR775 crores. In terms of our expansion plan, as we've always said, our annual cash accrual should be enough to sort of fund all the store openings and plans that we have.

items.statement: Revenue per sq ft flattish with inflation; growth depends on banner mix (Metro/Crocs vs others)
items.quote: I think flattish with some inflation at some point in time. But if we open up more Metro and Crocs stores, that is going to grow. If we open up other banners, it's not going to grow as fast

items.statement: Walkway brand positioning work in progress; closer to cracking it and accelerating growth
items.quote: we definitely feel that we're closer to cracking that and don't see any obstacles from where we sit today for us to get that banner growing.

items.statement: Aspiration to grow revenue more than double in next 5 years with substantial profitability margin increase
items.quote: Our aspiration is to grow the revenue to more than double in the next 5 years with profitability margin also seeing a substantial increase.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance of 11% to 13% maintained for FY25
items.quote: We ensured we remained within our previous communicated guidance of 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 7% to 9% maintained for FY25

items.statement: FY25 gross margin at 11.6% within guidance range
items.quote: Gross profit increased to INR 150 crores, up from INR 137 crores in FY '24, while achieving gross margin of 11.6% in FY '25, in -line with our given guidance of 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Non-lounge services expected to have 2-15% higher margins than current lounge margins

items.statement: Order book stands at ₹3,500 crore, entirely comprising AMISP-led smart meter projects.
items.quote: Today, the entire ₹3,500 crore order book comprises AMISP-led smart meter projects—providing multi-year visibility and a clear runway for execution.

items.statement: Targeting strong double-digit revenue growth in FY26; expects well over ₹1,000 crore of order book execution in FY26.
items.quote: We expect well over ₹1,000 crore worth of orders to be executed in FY26.

items.statement: Expects CapEx of around ₹100 crore in FY26, split between maintenance (₹30-35 crore) and growth across metering, switchgear, and wires & cables.
items.quote: To summarise, we expect CapEx of around ₹100 crore in FY26. This will be a mix of maintenance and growth investments.

items.statement: Guides for metering EBITDA margin of 17-18% and consumer/industrial margin of 11.5-12% in near term.
items.quote: For metering, we expect to stay in the 17–18 percent EBITDA margin range in the near term.

items.statement: Expects pricing pressure in smart metering as volumes scale and new players enter; plans to offset via automation, design optimization, and cost structure improvements.
items.quote: So yes, as new players enter the space and volumes grow, we do expect average prices to come down.

items.statement: Smart meter rollout momentum remains strong; national installation pace crossed 100,000 meters per day; expects FY26 execution to exceed FY25.
items.quote: In fact, I came across a recent update suggesting that the national rollout has crossed 100,000 meters per day, which is a very positive indicator for the sector and for us.

items.statement: Wires & cables grew ~24% YoY in FY25; domestic switchgear grew ~16%; lighting grew 6.6%; industrial switchgear saw softness but expects rebound in Q1/Q2 FY26.
items.quote: In FY25, growth in this segment was led by wires and cables, which delivered approximately 24 percent growth year-on-year. Domestic switchgear also performed well, growing by around 16 percent.

items.statement: Revenue dip risk stems from timing delays in smart meter execution (site readiness, approvals, dispatch clearances) at AMI SP end, not demand.
items.quote: A potential dip in revenue would most likely stem from timing-related delays in the smart metering segment.

items.statement: FY26 CapEx to be funded mainly through internal accruals and long-term term debt; no equity dilution indicated.
items.quote: Yeah, mainly through internal accruals and a certain term debt, long term debt.

items.statement: Smart meter capacity sufficient for next 3-4 quarters; modular infrastructure allows 3-4 month lead time for expansion if needed; not rushing to scale aggressively.
items.quote: At present, we have sufficient capacity to meet projected demand over the next three to four quarters.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 metering EBIT margin ~18.74% vs ~14% YoY; full-year FY25 metering EBIT margin ~17%; consumer/industrial EBITDA margin ~11.5% for FY25.
items.quote: On a full-year basis for FY25, EBIT margins for metering averaged around 17 percent, underscoring the margin uplift from the continued scale-up in smart meter adoption.

items.statement: Believes average quarterly run-rate of ₹500 crore achievable over next four quarters; Q1 typically softer, Q4 strongest for consumer/industrial; smart metering not seasonal.
items.quote: Broadly speaking, we believe an average quarterly run-rate of ₹500 crore is achievable over the next four quarters.

items.statement: Fan business crossed 100,000 unit shipments; targets 75% domestic market coverage by end of FY26, pan-India by next summer; onboarding 70-100 new channel partners.
items.quote: We have already crossed the 100,000-unit mark in terms of fan shipments, and the initial market feedback has been very encouraging.

items.statement: Receivable days improved to ~129 days (incl. GST) from 150-160 days earlier; expects further improvement in smart metering receivables; inventory days stable with marginal improvement.
items.quote: As a company, including the impact of GST, our current debtor days stand at approximately 129. This represents a notable improvement from earlier levels, where we were operating around 150 to 160 days.

items.statement: Estimates ~4-5 crore smart meters formally awarded as purchase orders out of 16 crore awarded to AMISPs; orders released in tranches based on supplier performance.

items.statement: Smart meter hardware accounts for ~30-40% of total AMISP project cost (approx. one-third each for meter, system infra, financing); expects meter costs to decline with scale.

items.statement: Revenue to grow at 45-50% CAGR over next two years, standalone, excluding acquisition.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue to double in FY26 including acquisition.
items.quote: If I take into account the contribution of the recent acquisition, I am very happy to share with you that our revenue would double in this financial year.

items.statement: Operating margins to improve in H1 FY26, then flat in H2 FY26 and FY27.

items.statement: Margin sustainability depends on pricing; cannot pinpoint 20% or 22%.
items.quote: See, it will all depend on the pricing. I mean what can I tell you? I mean, I can't pinpoint the number of 20%, 22%.

items.statement: US 10% import duties may impact business, but overall impact expected limited due to diversified sales footprint.

items.statement: US tariffs at 10% for now; real date is 9th July, uncertain whether it will come back to zero or remain at 10%.

items.statement: New electric arc furnace capacities in western economies require big ultra-high power electrodes, where competition from China is minimal.

items.statement: Domestic graphite anode demand expected 100,000 to 140,000 tons by 2030; first stage 20,000 tons, hope to double in next 4 to 5 years.

So our first stage, of course, we are starting with 20,000, but we hope that in the same location

items.statement: Demerger scheme filed with stock exchanges and authorities; expect all approvals by end of calendar year 2025.
items.quote: Our scheme has been filed with stock exchanges and all other relevant authorities, after which it will go to NCLT. We expect to get all the required approvals by end of calendar year 2025.

items.statement: Capacity utilization for FY25 close to 80% based on expanded capacity of 100,000 tons; hope to maintain or increase slightly in current year.
items.quote: Our capacity utilization for the year 2024-25 was close to 80% based on our expanded capacity of 100,000 tons and we hope to maintain this in the cu rrent year too, if not increase th is a little bit

items.statement: Focus on D2C, leisure, and retail; strong in corporate and student.
items.quote: The focus is on D2C, leisure and retail, because already we are strong in corporate and student.

items.statement: Launching multi-currency card variant shortly; sees it as big opportunity.
items.quote: We have launched the single currency card variant. We are shortly launching the multi-currency card variant and we are looking at it as a big opportunity both in terms of direct sales and channel sales.

items.statement: Will apply for PA-CB license within this quarter or before next quarter ends.

items.statement: Next 6-9 months focus on scaling Direct Card Issuance business.
items.quote: So next 6 months to 9 months, our focus will be on getting the Direct Card Issuance business into scale.

items.statement: Aim to increase platform usage from 50-60% to 80%.
items.quote: We need to see everything put together, but our idea is to slowly pivot from that 50%-60% level to the 80% level.

items.statement: Aim to card every student, take attachment rate to 100%.
items.quote: In fact, it has been a key focus for us to ensure that every student gets a card, whether the load is small or big, and that drive is on. Of course, today, you may say that is not 100%, but our aim is to take it to 100% levels.

items.statement: Aim to reach 80% of corporate business on platform.
items.quote: We have around close to 50% on the platform because bigger companies are more ready to get into the platform. There is some resistance by smaller companies. We are working on it, but our aim is to at least reach 80%.

items.statement: Student segment under pressure due to geopolitical situation and visa restrictions.
items.quote: As you are all aware, student segment is under a little bit of pressure because of the geopolitical situation.

items.statement: TCS guidelines impact business; ticket size reduced.
items.quote: One of the impacts which has been there for the last 1, 1.5 years has been the TCS guidelines where there is a TCS of 5% and 20% when it comes to personal remittances in travel.

items.statement: Corporate business not growing as fast as anticipated, still below pre-COVID levels.
items.quote: Corporate business where we have a key strength, is not growing as fast as we would have anticipated because it's still not reached the pre-COVID levels because of technology and collaboration through VCs etc.

items.statement: Leisure travel seen as biggest opportunity, validated by LRS numbers.
items.quote: We feel growth in leisure travel is the biggest opportunity as of now and it's als o validated by the LRS numbers

items.statement: FXC opportunity anticipated this year, pending RBI approval.
items.quote: Now this is something which has not still come through, but we are hopeful that this year it will come through, which will ensure that we have distribution reach through this network.

items.statement: Working on platform for seamless student fee payments.
items.quote: We are also working on a platform which will help the students fo r making the fees seamlessly and that's one activity w hich we are working on

items.quote: We are also working with leading expense management companies like Zaggle. We have also got some 200-300 agents who are working with us.

items.quote: So still we have some deferred tax in the asset which is around Rs. 2 crores or so. So in the next year, when it will be utilized that time it will be reversed.

items.statement: Tax rate applicable is 22% plus surcharge, so 25%.
items.quote: It is 22%, right plus surcharge, so 25%.

items.statement: Standalone EMS and BTS to grow at blended rate of 25% to 28%.
items.quote: And we expect that growth momentum to continue , and basically at a standalone level both the EMS and the BTS part of the business should grow for us at a blended rate of somewhere in the range of about 25% to 28%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue to grow 18% to 20%.
items.quote: Yes. On a consolidated basis, we will grow for 18% to 20%, and that is basically driven by a higher growth rate contribution from the standalone entity, which is at over the 25% level, whereas at the subsidiary level we would be roughly flat, I would say.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 10% possible.
items.quote: Yes. That should be definitely be possible at the consol level.

items.statement: Goal to improve consolidated EBITDA margin to around 12% in next two years.
items.quote: Yes. Definitely. I think that's our goal, to improve that from 10% to probably around 12% in the next two years.

items.statement: Targeting 18% to 20% CAGR for next three years.
items.quote: As we have been maintaining, we are targeting 18% to 20% CAGR for the next three years.

items.statement: Planning to invest Rs. 40 crores in standalone capex for FY26.
items.quote: Okay. We are planning to invest about Rs. 40 crores, that again only in the standalone, essentially to augment the capabilities and increase the capacities, both in the BTS segment as well as the EMS segment.

items.statement: Targeting Rs. 2,000 crores of order booking in next three to four years.
items.quote: The pipeline of orders is healthy, I mentioned this in the past, we are roughly looking at something in the range of about Rs. 2,000 crores of booking in the next three to four years, that's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Typical EBITDA margin for build-to-spec around 20%, EMS 10-12%.
items.quote: So, your typical EBITDA margin for build-to-spec can be in the range of 20% or so . And whereas on the EMS side of the business, it's more build-to-print, and that is typically in the 10% to 12% level or so.

items.quote: So, there will be something that we are doing and we are targeting to have this completed by September or sooner.

items.quote: It will not continue. It is only for the last year. In FY '26, the confusion between gross and net accounting will not be there.

items.statement: Expects substantial revenues and billing from electronic intelligence program this year.
items.quote: And we expect this year that we will have substantial revenues and billing from this program as well.

items.statement: Order book executable over 15 to 18 months overall.
items.quote: And maybe at an overall basis something in the range of about 15 months or so, 15 odd months I would say, 15 to 18 months is what you can look at.

items.statement: Confident of achieving $450 million top line, 16% EBITDA, and 30% return on capital employed in FY26.
items.value: $450 million, 16% EBITDA, 30% return on capital employed
items.quote: We have given a guidance for 25-26 as part of our five year guidance that we did five years ago. We are quite confident that we will hit that that you know, I don't want to get into aggressive and conservative, but that's really our projection which is $450 million of top line revenue. 16% EBITDA and 30% return on capital employed.

items.statement: India expected to grow low to mid double digit if economy remains whole and no global tariff impact.
items.quote: So assuming India remains whole economically and there is no impact of tariffs globally. I expect India to grow double digit, but I would probably say low to mid double digit.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth expected at minimum same as last year's 9% if steady state.
items.quote: Will next year be better than this. Again, I don't want to put anything on the ground because a lot of uncertainties at the moment with respect to the US tariff and its impact. Rippling impact on the various economies. Of the world, assuming it is, everything comes back to a steady state. Nothing negative, and India continues to be a good story. We should be able to do this. Minimum do this same g

items.statement: Confident of hitting 16% EBITDA margin as one-time expenses won't repeat.
items.quote: As far as profitability is concerned, we will hit. We were already hitting close to 16% even this year manish. It is just that one-time expenses and clean up that we did that dropped out EBITDA. So what is going to happen is that is not going to get repeated. In next year. And therefore, we're quite confident that we'll be able to hit those numbers.

items.statement: Can absorb 10% tariff without impacting profitability due to motor plant savings.
items.quote: For 26 the assuming, 10% tariff we have like I explained to you, we will be able to absorb that 10% without any impact on our profitability, because the savings that we have from our motor plant and a few other initiatives that we kicked off almost couple of years ago for cost reduction is more than enough to absorb it.

items.statement: Can sustain current pricing and profitability up to 16% reciprocal tariff.
items.quote: And assuming they are going to make it in the worst-case reciprocal to that same percentage in this range, we are pretty much ok with all the cost reduction initiatives we can sustain our current pricing and our profitability.

items.statement: If US moves to 26% tariff, may need to increase prices or find other ways.
items.quote: But if they move to 26% like they originally did, then that could be we need to make a decision in terms of either increasing prices or finding other ways as we speak all our competitors.

items.statement: Portable compressors expected to remain subdued in current year due to market drop.
items.quote: Portables is a more a market structural thing. items.statement: Stabilizer and Chinese-import-competing machines to be fully launched by Q3.
items.quote: Our machines for competing with the Chinese Imports are already working in the field and we are confident that by the third quarter both these products will be out in the market full-fledged and our earlier initiative called Project Everest for increasing our share of the market is going very well.

items.statement: Aftermarket share in India 27-28%, rest of world 13-14%, expected to improve.
items.quote: It's about 27-28% is on our revenue in India in the rest of the world, we are probably around 13 to 14% right now in both these percentages have to keep improving as we progress through the life cycle of life of the of the. Operation, I mean I we get more and more machines installed then there is more and more aftermarket coming in.

items.statement: Motor plant capacity not an issue; machines being installed after visa delays.
items.quote: So now that is opened up and the machines are getting installed. So we're quite confident. That we have the capacity. That's not an issue.

items.statement: Siemens railway business to see movement in Q3 and Q4, significant improvement next year.
items.quote: So I think we will see some movement of the business during the third and fourth quarter of this year. But I think next year we will see more of a significant you know improvement in the in that model of compressors and locomotives.

items.statement: Europe faces tariff uncertainty; will watch Q1 and adjust cost structure if needed.
items.quote: But the only caution here now is the Tariff other than that, we are not pretty strong wicket, right. But we are watching the situation very carefully. We are not going to invest anything more, right. What we are going to do is in response to any, if there is any challenges, we will look at cost structure changes, not in terms of you know this Willy nilly. reduction in cost, but structurally change

items.quote: So barring the one time clean-up cost that we had did on inventory and receivables, even in the US besides other parts of the world Harshit, the operations was actually profitable, right? So US has from a loss in the prior year has actually become profitable on a steady state basis now.

items.statement: Expects good growth in India and US, Europe uncertain, Australia recovering.
items.quote: So, India will be assuming the economic Structure remains solid. We will have good growth in India and we are confident of that. US is going to come back because it really hit the bottom. So we're confident that it'll come back from the past. Europe is a question mark at the moment, it is still showing signs of positivity. Australia's coming back.

items.statement: Announced INR 1,400 million investment for new HVDC Thyristor and VSC Valves manufacturing line and HVDC Controls facility.
items.quote: Recognizing this opportunity and our role in enabling India's energy transition, earlier this month we announced a strategic investment of INR 1,400 million. items.statement: Pricing is stable; no incremental growth, but can pass on raw material price increases.
items.quote: So I would say that the pricing is stable as of now. Maybe we don't see much improvement coming there. If there is an increase in raw material prices, we are able to pass on. items.statement: Expects 1-2 HVDC projects to be decided this year.
items.quote: But we expect at least 1 to 2 projects to get decided during this year.

items.statement: Strategy to move towards product orders rather than turnkey projects for better margins.
items.quote: And as a strategy, we are moving towards product orders and -- rather than focusing on turnkey orders that leads to a better margin profile.

items.statement: Supply chain is a big challenge due to global demand explosion.
items.quote: Supply chain, yes, definitely, today in this very uncertain world, supply chain is a big challenge. And with the explosion of demand globally, yes.

items.statement: No plans to backward integrate component manufacturing.

items.quote: During the entire year, we have made a royalty payment of roughly INR640 million.

items.statement: Service revenue is sub-10% of total revenue.
items.quote: Generally, the service revenue is sub -10% for us.

items.quote: We are positive that in the next two years, we will make sure that we don't have to pay any tax and the deferred tax asset would be used for that.

items.quote: But in general, about 60% overall gross margin is what the company targets. And we are normally somewhere close to that.

items.quote: So when you're talking about ₹400 crores to ₹500 crores, that's the size, including the equipment.

items.quote: So you can say in general, if you sell a line for ₹100, normally the AMC charge would be ₹15 to ₹20, would be the software charges, which would be a recurring charge after the first year.

items.statement: Expects operational losses in packaging to reduce over the year.

items.quote: So we definitely expect that to reduce over the course of the year, like if you look at the overall annual basis.

items.statement: Expects revenue growth to help curtail consolidated losses.
items.quote: But we expect the revenue growth to kick in to some extent. And obviously, the margin on that revenue should be good, and that should help curtail the consolidated losses.

items.quote: And we know that the industry is going to grow at about 9%, 10%, 11%. Let's take it as 10%. We believe we've got a slightly better product mix. So we should do 10%, maybe a bit more.

items.statement: FY26 revenue and profit trajectory expected in same range as FY25.

items.statement: Pune JV volumes to ramp up fully from second and third quarter onward.
items.quote: But from the second and third quarter onward, it will be ramped up fully.

items.statement: Debt levels for coming financial year to remain same as March 2025.

items.statement: Plans to add 15 to 20 products in FY26.

items.statement: Dehradun plant capacity utilization expected to ramp up to 50-55%.
items.quote: The Dehradun plant is expected to ramp up, say, around 50% to 55%.

items.statement: Mumbai plant capacity utilization expected around 70-75%.
items.quote: On the Mumbai plant, we prefer keeping the plant around 70% to 75% level, which was there in previous quarters. We expect it to be around that level.

items.statement: Capex of INR3-4 crores incurred in FY25 for existing plants.
items.quote: We have incurred a capex of INR3 crores to INR4 crores during the financial year '25 for the existing plants.

items.statement: Capex for Pune plant in FY25 was INR30-35 crores.
items.quote: So the capex for the Pune plant was in the range of INR30 crores to INR35 crores.

items.statement: Pune facility has order book covering next 90 days.
items.quote: The facility already has a robust order book that covers the next 90 days.

items.statement: No exact margins guidance for FY26.
items.quote: Ma'am, we wouldn't be giving or sharing the exact margins as of now.

items.statement: Growth expected from French African market later in FY26; focus on Middle East and Latin America for next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: Ideally, we expect growth to come in from there, but that will be on the later end of the FY '26. For the current 2 to 3 quarters, we are majorly focused on to our existing markets in the Middle East and the Latin American zone.

items.statement: Product mix of injectable versus oral expected to remain same in FY26.
items.quote: So the mix should remain the same only.

items.statement: US tariff announcements and push for local manufacturing may impact capex decisions near term.

items.statement: International Supply Chain capex approximately less than INR50 crores to INR60 crores.

items.quote: The International Supply Chain should be approximately about INR30 crores for this -- yes. So I mean, it should be approximately about less than INR50 crores to INR60 crores on the International Supply Chain business with all these investments put together.

items.statement: No significant capital expenditure expected in FY26 for non-IT.
items.quote: And FY '26 as well, non-IT, we do not see any significant capital expenditure.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions expected to last at least another 3 months.
items.quote: So all over, well, our expectation is at least it takes another 3 months until we have a normalized situation.

items.statement: Momentum picking up in demand, with significant demand already coming in.
items.quote: But at this point in time, there is a momentum picking up in demand. items.statement: Short-term volatility in freight rates expected for key trade lanes.
items.quote: And there could be some short-term volatility in the freight rate for some of the key trade lanes.

items.statement: Contract logistics margin to improve but remain below historical averages.
items.quote: So the in-season white spaces, which has happened, the reversal should lead to an improvement in the margin profile, but it would continue to remain below the historical averages wherein chemical contract logistics used to be a significant part.

items.statement: NCLT final hearing expected first week of July; relisting process 2-4 months after.
items.quote: We have our next, which potentially could be the final hearing with NCLT in the first week of July. And from there on, typically, in our estimate, it should be about anywhere between 2 months, 2, 3.5, 4 months kind of a process.

items.statement: Gross debt on international supply chain business approximately INR500 crores.
items.quote: Yes. So the gross debt on the international supply chain business would be approximately INR500 crores.

items.statement: Working capital debt INR800-900 crores gross; long-term borrowing INR200 crores India side.
items.quote: So all put together, if you look at the gross level, almost INR800 crores to INR900 crores ballpark is in the short-term or the working capital debt.

items.statement: Reduction in working capital driven by improved collections and reduced DSO.

items.statement: Expanding global pooling to offset interest payments.
items.quote: Yes. So we're expanding our usage of global pooling with our primary bank at this stage, which is enabling us to then to extract funds from the regions into our Central Bank, which we can then use to offset the interest payments.

items.statement: Evaluating supplier trade credit and factoring to release cash.
items.quote: In addition to that, from a working capital point of view, we're evaluating additional options for releasing cash such as supplier trade credit programs. And we're also looking into strategies potentially around some factoring.

items.statement: Capacity shifts may cause port congestion and supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: Higher demand and rates help increase volumes and revenues.

items.statement: Invested in CFS in Korea for consolidation and deconsolidation space.

items.statement: Defense expected to contribute around 5% of revenue in medium to long term.

items.statement: Defense and exports together to contribute 9% to 10% in FY26.

items.statement: May revise guidance by end of Q2 FY26 depending on industry conditions.

items.statement: Expects to achieve INR4,400 crores revenue by FY27.

And in saying that, obviously, we have targ eted and had conveyed that we will do it in 3 years, but like you're saying, yes, definitely, it will be exceeded and it will be 4 years, but it should definitely be exceeded in 4 years. I'm sure we will exceed INR4,400

items.statement: Sees sluggishness in inquiries and orders in Q1 FY26 due to price increases and rental segment negotiations.
items.quote: So there is really no pickup or improvement in inquiries or orders rather so far in this quarter there has been sluggishness in the inquiries as well as orders.

items.statement: Plans to increase market share in new generation cranes by 3-4% this year.
items.quote: But I'm sure within this year, we should be able to increase at least 3% 4% in the new generation trade, which are lemon green in color now.

items.statement: Agri division margins at 3.73%, working to improve.
items.quote: The Agri division registered revenue of around INR230 crores with margins at 3.73%.

items.statement: Net capex of Rs 50 crore and gross capex of Rs 75 crore in FY25; expects around Rs 75 crore capex in each of the next two years
items.quote: So roughly, I think last year we did a net CAPEX of 50, gross CAPEX of 75. This year we would probably do around 75 in CAPEX and probably the year after that also we would be at 75 because we have a good amount of capacity coming in into lightweighting as well as our customers are moving in the west of India.

items.statement: Received almost all targeted orders for TREM-V; export order for CV emission components from world's largest engine manufacturer to start production in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Yes, so we have received almost all orders that we had to in terms of the target for TREM-V. However, there is an ongoing conversation between the tractor industry and the government, which we are not privy to.

items.statement: Export order for commercial vehicle emission components from world's largest engine manufacturer and a genset manufacturer to go into production in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We have received a substantial award, which we had announced previously, for emission components for commercial vehicles. And that will go into production in Q4 of this year. It is for the world's largest engine manufacturer, as well as a genset manufacturer.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 14% from 12.9% in FY24; Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin was 13.4%
items.quote: On a full year basis, EBITDA was Rs. 396.37 crores, up 9.7% over FY'24 with a margin of 14% in FY'25 versus 12.9% in FY'24.

items.quote: So roughly 88 % came from emissions, 9 % to 10 % came from lightweighting and the balance 1%-2% is others.

items.statement: Off-highway, CV and LCV revenue share currently ~45% (slightly under 50%), target is 80%; lightweighting contributes ~9-10% and is powertrain agnostic

items.quote: No, these norms have come in and it's just that the inventory is there in Q 1, Q2 with the construction equipment companies and they will clear that off. So, and that's why we have said that the real production will really start from Q3.

items.statement: Board approved 1:1 bonus shares and dividend of Rs 32.5 per share in May 2025 board meeting
items.quote: In the recently concluded board meeting on 24 th of May, the Board has approved the issue of bonus shares in the ratio of 1 is to 1, in addition to dividend of Rs. 32.5 per share.

items.statement: Actively pursuing inorganic opportunities via technical agreements, JVs, and acquisitions; dedicated M&A team formed in last 12 months focusing on powertrain agnostic components and exponential growth markets
items.quote: Yes, we are looking at it, right? And we have a significant cash surplus, though when we look at inorganic, I would just like to take it in 2-3 things, which is technical agreements, joint ventures and acquisitions. We have a separate team who is working on that.

items.statement: Advises tracking gross profit growth (11% YoY in FY25) rather than revenue growth (1% YoY) due to catalyst pass-through impact; working on alternative reporting mechanism for clarity
items.quote: So the best way to look at our underlying growth is gross profit and not the sales number and that's because of the catalyst and that has a big impact due to catalyst prices and mix. So if you look at it, our gross profit growth year-on-year has been 11% versus the PV industry growth at roughly 3%-3.5%.

items.quote: This year if you look at it, we have won some new lightweighting programs So that will come in between Q3 and Q4 which we have shared in our investor presentation then our new plant the suspension plant which we had put Chakan Plant-3 that is coming into production. So that should really start getting into revenues. Then we also have won an order for temperature control pipes, which is an adjacenc

items.quote: Thank you. So first in terms of CAPEX, we will be in the range of about Rs. 75 crores for the next two years in terms of CAPEX.

items.quote: So depreciation is nothing but our new plant coming in for lightweighting and that's adding to the depreciation and the CAPEX cycle and that is only depreciation front. But for us, where the main drivers have been, that there are consultants now that we have in US

items.quote: Control arms, So, the light weighting, so definitely we do seem to increase further market share in control arms. You we are just getting going in lightweighting the way I would like to put it, right? Howev

items.statement: Expects around 25% plus revenue growth in the coming year.
items.quote: So going forward also and we are quite optimistic to cross this average of growth basically, so maybe around 25% plus growth, we will see in the coming year also.

items.quote: Looking at the future, we are planning a capital expenditure of Rs. 50-Rs. 60 crores over the next 2-3 years, primarily towards establishing a dedicated manufacturing facility for the WPC Doors and enhancing capacity at our Southern India plants.

items.statement: Maintains healthy order book of over Rs. 140 crores in project business.
items.quote: We continue to maintain a healthy order book of over Rs. 140 crores in our project-related business, which now accounts for approximately 30% of our overall revenues.

items.statement: Confident margins can be easily maintained going forward.
items.quote: So we are confident that the margins can be easily maintained going forward also.

items.statement: Plans to take fluted and soffit segment to Rs. 100 crores in 2-3 years.
items.quote: Rs. 100 crores, just our plan is to do it in within 2 years, next 2 years maybe, or you can take it 2-3 years we will achieve, take this segment to Rs. 100 crores level.

items.statement: Plans around Rs. 15 crores capex in current year if WPC Door project starts.
items.quote: Yes, each year that this particular year, we can take around Rs. 15 crores of CAPEX if the things get speed up because we are working on a certain new product addition as mentioned at the WPC Door.

items.statement: Plans to increase exhibition and sales promotion spend to 2% of topline.
items.quote: Yes. See, last year we spent around 1.4% of our overall revenue on the exhibition and sales promotion activities. And we have a plan to take it to the 2% of topline.

items.statement: Plans to add two more Studio Arezzo stores in FY26.
items.quote: Yes, for the current Financial Year '26, we have planned for two more studio, Arezzo Studio to be added.

items.statement: Plans to be debt free in next 4-5 years.
items.quote: So considering the profitability and incremental business, so that CAPEX can be met out mostly with the internal accruals and at the same time, our vision to be debt free in the next 4-5 years can also be easily achieved.

items.statement: Plans to meet expansion capex through internal accruals.
items.quote: Otherwise, as of now, we have planned to meet this expansion plan through internal accruals only.

items.statement: Current capacity can generate Rs. 450-500 crores revenue.
items.quote: At the current capacity, revenue generation of around Rs. 450-Rs. 500 crores is really possible

items.statement: Planned capex will contribute additional Rs. 150-200 crores topline.
items.quote: So once that is implemented, so that will definitely contribute around Rs. 150-Rs. 200 crores of topline.

items.statement: Average cost of debt is less than 8.5% for both long and short term.
items.quote: Both, rate of interest is same, basically for both long term and short term, lesser than 8.5%.

items.statement: Added more than 15 sales heads last year.
items.quote: In fact, in last year also, we have added more than 15 heads in sales front.

items.statement: Around 40% revenue comes from South India.
items.quote: So we can say around 40% revenue is coming from the South India itself.

items.statement: Confident of double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin improvement in FY26.
items.quote: And as far as looking ahead in the guidance for financial '26, I think we are very confident of achieving double-digit growth going forward in next financial year. And also, we are very hopeful of improving our EBITDA from this level also.

items.statement: May revise guidance upwards in Q2 if expectations are met.
items.quote: Yes, we can revise our guidance in Q2 con call. So, if we see that everything is going as per the expectation, we may revise our guidance upwards in Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Plan to open 45-50 Monte Carlo stores and 10-15 Clock & Decker stores this year.
items.value: 45 to 50 Monte Carlo stores and 10 to 15 Clock & Decker stores
items.quote: So, this year also, we have plan to open 45 to 50 Monte Carlo stores and 10 to 15 Clock & Decker stores. And so, the speed will continue, I think, going forward for next 2 years.

items.quote: Viraj, you're right, we just concluded our 7-day winter trade show and the response was very good. We had more than 1,500 retailers coming over for the trade show and we've gotten a very good order book.

items.statement: Took 8-10% price hike this year; brand has pricing power to pass on prices.
items.quote: So last year, across all categories on average, 6% to 8% price hike was taken. And this year, 8% to 10% price hike was taken.

items.statement: April was muted but May saw recovery; expects good year ahead due to favorable macro factors.
items.quote: So, we begin this year with a muted start. So, April was not that great. But May, we begin very well. And we have seen some of the sales recovery, which we lost in April has happened in May as far as EBO levels are concerned.

items.quote: But definitely, winter wear has been a very huge segment. So, it might take 1 or 2 more years for a company to have around 45% to 55% ratio. But as of now, I think we have reached almost 30%, 35% of summer wear sales, including total garment sale in whole year.

items.statement: Q4 discounts and returns caused loss; will take adequate provisioning to make Q4 zero level.
items.quote: But we'll make sure that, again, this financial year, we take adequate provisioning to make at least at a zero level for fourth quarter.

items.statement: Expects 5-10 days reduction in debtor days from tying up with distributors.
items.quote: We expect 5 to 10 days of debtor days should come down going forward.

items.statement: Inventory will remain at current level plus/minus 5%.
items.quote: So, in that case, we don't see a very significant improvement in the inventory level, but it will remain at this level, plus/minus 5%.

items.quote: And we've also tied up with Style, which is from the Landmark Group in the UAE, to supply around 8,000 to 10,000 pieces of Monte Carlo products in the UAE market.

items.statement: Plans to shut down 150 MBOs in West Bengal and Northeast and open EBOs instead.
items.quote: And so, what we've taken a call is we are going to shut down these 150-odd MBO outlets and instead open our own exclusive brand outlets to service these markets.

items.statement: Sunroof JV revenues will start from FY27, not FY26.

items.statement: Flash Electronics revenue growth expected in mid-to-high double-digit percentage.
items.quote: So Raghu, the growth momentum in the revenue of Flash Electronics should be again in the similar range that they have been doing for the last few years. So, again, in the range of mid - to high double -digit percentage.

items.statement: Capex to remain INR 250-350 crores; Flash capex INR 50-100 crores.
items.value: INR 250 crores to max INR 350 crores
items.quote: Going forward, we see the capex to remain in the range of about INR 250 crores to max INR 350 crores. And as regards the capex in Flash is concerned, again, that should broadly be in the range of INR 50 crores to INR 100 crores only.

items.statement: Lifetime orders over INR 8,000 crores, with 25% from EV platforms.
items.quote: During the year, the Company booked lifetime orders exceeding INR 8,000 crores with approximately 25% of new orders coming from electric vehicle platforms.

items.statement: Highest-ever EBITDA margin of 11.6% in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: The Company reported highest-ever EBITDA of INR 153 crores, along with the highest ever margin of 11.6% for the quarter, demonstrating strong operational execution and the effectiveness of our strategic initiatives.

items.statement: EV sales were 8% of Q4 revenue and 7% for full year.
items.quote: In Q4, EV sales stood at about 8% of the Minda Corporation's total revenue and on a full year basis, it is approximately 7%.

items.statement: Digital clusters to grow to 40% of instrument cluster business in 18-24 months.
items.quote: So currently about INR 800 crores plus revenue of the Minda Instruments Limited, you can say the digital clusters contribute somewhere about 25% to 30% and, of course, this is expected to grow to somewhere about 40% or so in the next, let's say, 18 months to 24 months.

items.statement: PAT impacted by higher finance costs from Flash investment and increased depreciation.
items.quote: This was impacted by higher finance costs associated with the strategic investment in flash electronics and increased depreciation stemming from ongoing capacity expansion and technolog ical upgrades.

items.statement: Promoter investment at INR 550 per share; 25% in 2 weeks, 75% in 18 months.
items.quote: We are expecting the stock exchanges approval within this week, and 25% of the money should be received max within 2 weeks and thereafter, as per the terms, the balance 75% can be paid by the promoters within 18 months.

items.statement: Sensors revenue for FY25 is INR 250-300 crores, expected to grow.

items.statement: Cross-selling with Flash to reach close to 3-digit number by FY27.
items.quote: And by FY27, we can see maybe close to a 3-digit number coming into cross-selling.

items.statement: Localization of Minda connectors to reach 20-25% in 18-24 months.
items.quote: Our target is to reach about 20% to 25% over the next 18 to 24 months. All efforts are in those directions.

items.statement: Debt to equity target reduced to 0.2x in 2-3 years.
items.quote: So, yes, the interest is how we can bring down the 0.5x debt to equity to about 0.2x in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Utilization currently at 65-80% across organization.
items.quote: But overall, we, as an organization, are currently working to the tune of about 65% to 80% of utilization. So different segments, different plants will have that variation.

items.statement: Flash Electronics FY25 revenue INR 1,537 crores, EBITDA margin 14.5%.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins in low 20s as initial goal, with established centers over 20% and emerging centers improving toward that level
items.quote: But is it good to say as the emerging centers also rack up, our margin, as we always indicated, will be in the low 20s. That is our initial goal.

items.statement: Expect more than 20% EBITDA margin in future from current portfolio, but new center operationalization may cause dilution until scale-up
items.quote: In our current portfolio, we should be expecting more than 20% in the future to come in the near future. However, as we operationalize new centres as part of our expansion initiative, overall we may see dilution till these centres scale up to steady state.

items.quote: Looking ahead, we plan a capex of INR286 crores in FY '26 in line with our network expansion and technology upgrade plans.

items.statement: Capex of INR286 crores in FY26 includes ~INR100 crores maintenance capex and growth capex in existing centers and markets like Bangalore and Cuttack
items.quote: I think it is in the range of about INR 280 crores. We already invested a little over INR200 crores in last financial year. That includes close to about INR100 crores of maintenance capex and large growth capex within our existing centers and markets are in Bangalore and Cuttack.

items.statement: Aim to operationalize over 900 beds across network within next 3 years, including 350 beds fully invested but not yet operational
items.quote: As informed earlier, we aim to expand in our existing markets by operationalizing over 900 beds across networks within next 3 years, including this year's addition and 350 beds that are fully invested but not yet operational.

items.quote: You would notice that we have over 20% margin in our established centers, showcasing the strength of the platform. However, our emerging centers are a little over 10%. Together, we are delivering close to about 18% margin.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to improve as emerging centers scale toward established center margins, driven by operating leverage
items.quote: As our emerging centers continue to grow, which is again reflected in last year's performance, you will see that our revenue grew by 32% and our EBITDA has grown by 44% in the same quarter for emerging centers, reflecting an increase in EBITDA margin as well.

items.statement: ARPOB increased 4% YoY to INR44,236 in Q4 FY25; established centers ARPOB INR42,591 (+2.5%), emerging centers INR66,755 (+12.4%)
items.quote: On the pricing and efficiency front, for the quarter ended 31st March '25, ARPOB across our network increased by 4%, reaching to INR 44,236. Established center recorded an ARPOB of INR42,591 growing by 2.5%, while emerging centers delivered an impressive ARPOB of INR66,755, growing by 12.4%.

items.statement: Expect 7-8% ARPOB growth in FY26 driven by decreasing length of stay and high-end treatment modalities
items.quote: With continu ous decrease in length of stay in the hospital coupled with high end treatment modalities we expect 7% to 8% increase in ARPOB

items.quote: In medical oncology, we saw a 24% growth in chemotherapy sessions, a clear indicator of growing patient demand. Our LINAC machine utilization remained steady at 60% in quarter 4 of FY '25 with acquisition of 2 LINACs with MGM Hospital over the last 12 months.

items.statement: Digital revenue doubled in FY25; launched HCG mobile app for appointments, virtual consults, reports; expect digital to become major revenue contributor
items.quote: Digital revenue for FY '25 has doubled over the past year, and we are committed to scaling this further. We launched our official HCG mobile app, a platform that enables to book appointments, consult doctor virtually, access reports and manage their care journey end-to-end.

items.statement: Plan to divest Milann fertility business this fiscal year after addressing partner competition issues and discussing with new investor KKR
items.quote: We have addressed this issue internally. We were just waiting for the new investor also to come. We have also discussed with them. So, we are definitely putting a proposal to divest. And hopefully, this will happen definitely this fiscal year, and we'll keep you updated.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected around 30% for FY26
items.quote: I think we can expect about 30-odd percent to remain in that level during the next 1 year.

items.statement: Global supply chain disruptions and low-grade business environment compressed margins.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected at 25% with EBITDA margin 21% plus/minus 100 basis points.

items.statement: Average revenue growth of 25% year-on-year expected over next three years.

items.statement: Clean energy sector expected to grow 15-20% in FY26.
